chapters: In the beginning Elokim created the heavens and the earth.
And the earth was unformed and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep, and the spirit of Elokim was hovering upon the face of the waters.
And Elokim said: Let there be light, and there was light.
And Elokim saw the light that it was good, and Elokim divided between the light and between the darkness.
And Elokim called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night, and there was evening and there was morning, one day.
And Elokim said: Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide between water and water.
And Elokim made the firmament, and Elokim divided between the waters that are under the firmament and between the waters that are above the firmament, and it was so.
And Elokim called the firmament Heavens, and there was evening and there was morning, the second day.
And Elokim said: Let the waters under the heavens be gathered to one place, and let the dry land appear, and it was so.
And Elokim called the dry land Earth, and the gathering of the waters He called Seas, and Elokim saw that it was good.
And Elokim said: Let the earth sprout grass, seed-bearing herbs, and fruit trees bearing fruit of their kind, whose seed is in them upon the earth, and it was so.
And the earth brought forth grass, seed-bearing herbs of their kind, and fruit trees bearing fruit whose seed is in them, of their kind, and Elokim saw that it was good.
And there was evening and there was morning, the third day.
And Elokim said: Let there be lights in the firmament of the heavens to divide between the day and between the night, and let them be for signs and for appointed times and for days and years.
And let them be for lights in the firmament of the heavens to give light upon the earth, and it was so.
And Elokim made the two great lights: the great light to rule the day, and the small light to rule the night, and the stars.
And Elokim set them in the firmament of the heavens to give light upon the earth.
And to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide between the light and between the darkness, and Elokim saw that it was good.
And there was evening and there was morning, the fourth day.
And Elokim said: Let the waters swarm with swarms of living souls, and let birds fly over the earth, across the face of the firmament of the heavens.
And Elokim created the great sea-creatures, and every living soul that crawls, with which the waters swarmed, of their kinds, and every winged bird of its kind, and Elokim saw that it was good.
And Elokim blessed them, saying: Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds multiply on the earth.
And there was evening and there was morning, the fifth day.
And Elokim said: Let the earth bring forth living souls of every kind, cattle and creeping things and beasts of the earth of every kind, and it was so.
And Elokim made the wild beasts of the earth of every kind, and the cattle of every kind, and every creeping thing of the ground of every kind, and Elokim saw that it was good.

And Elokim said: Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over the cattle and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that crawls upon the earth.
And Elokim created man in His image, in the image of Elokim He created him, male and female He created them.

And Elokim blessed them, and Elokim said to them: Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it, and rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over every living thing that crawls upon the earth.

And Elokim said: Behold, I have given to you every seed-bearing herb that is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree in which there is fruit of a tree bearing seed — to you it shall be for food.

And to every beast of the earth, and to every bird of the heavens, and to everything that crawls upon the earth, in which there is a living soul, I have given every green herb for food, and it was so.
And Elokim saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good, and there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.
And the heavens and the earth and all their host were completed.
And Elokim completed on the seventh day His work that He had made, and He rested on the seventh day from all His work that He had made.
And Elokim blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, for on it He rested from all His work that Elokim created to make.
These are the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, on the day Havayah Elokim made earth and heavens.

And every shrub of the field, before it was in the earth, and every herb of the field, before it sprouted, for Havayah Elokim had not yet caused rain upon the earth, and there was no man to work the ground.
And a mist would go up from the earth and water all the face of the ground.
And Havayah Elokim formed the man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils breath of life, and the man became a living soul.
And Havayah Elokim planted a garden in Eden, in the east, and He placed there the man whom He had formed.
And Havayah Elokim caused to sprout from the ground every tree pleasant to the sight and good for food, and the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
And a river goes out from Eden to water the garden, and from there it parts and becomes four heads.
The name of the one is Pishon, it is the one that surrounds all the land of Chavilah, where there is the gold.
And the gold of that land is good, there is the bdellium and the stone of onyx.
And the name of the second river is Gihon, it is the one that surrounds all the land of Kush.
And the name of the third river is Chidekel, it is the one that goes toward the east of Ashur, and the fourth river is Peras.
And Havayah Elokim took the man, and placed him in the garden of Eden to work it and to guard it.
And Havayah Elokim commanded the man, saying: From every tree of the garden you may eat freely.
And from the tree of knowledge of good and evil, you shall not eat from it, for on the day you eat from it, you shall surely die.
And Havayah Elokim said: It is not good for the man to be alone, I will make for him a helper opposite him.

And Havayah Elokim formed from the ground every beast of the field and every bird of the heavens, and brought them to the man to see what he would call it, and all that the man would call it, a living soul, that is its name.
And the man called names for all the cattle, and for the bird of the heavens, and for every beast of the field, but for Adam, he did not find a helper opposite him.
And Havayah Elokim cast a deep sleep upon the man, and he slept, and He took one of his sides, and closed flesh in its place.
And Havayah Elokim built the side that He took from the man into a woman, and brought her to the man.
And the man said: This time, bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh, this one shall be called Woman, for from man she was taken.
Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.
And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and they were not ashamed.
And the serpent was cunning more than every beast of the field that Havayah Elokim had made, and he said to the woman: Did Elokim really say: You shall not eat from every tree of the garden?
And the woman said to the serpent: From the fruit of the trees of the garden we may eat.
And from the fruit of the tree that is in the midst of the garden, Elokim said: You shall not eat from it and you shall not touch it, lest you die.
And the serpent said to the woman: You shall surely not die.
For Elokim knows that on the day you eat from it, your eyes shall be opened, and you shall be as Elokim, knowing good and evil.

And the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and the tree was desirable for gaining wisdom, and she took from its fruit and ate, and gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.
And the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they sewed leaves of fig and made for themselves loincloths.
And they heard the voice of Havayah Elokim walking in the garden in the breeze of the day, and the man and his wife hid from before Havayah Elokim among the trees of the garden.
And Havayah Elokim called the man, and said to him: Where are you?
And he said: Your voice I heard in the garden, and I was afraid, for I am naked, and I hid.
And He said: Who told you that you are naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?
And the man said: The woman whom You gave to be with me, she gave me from the tree, and I ate.
And Havayah Elokim said to the woman: What is this you have done? And the woman said: The serpent enticed me, and I ate.

And Havayah Elokim said to the serpent: Because you did this, cursed are you from all the cattle and from all the beast of the field, upon your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life.
And I will place enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed, he shall strike you on the head, and you shall strike him on the heel.
To the woman He said: I will greatly increase your pain and your pregnancy, in pain you shall bear children, and to your husband shall be your desire, and he shall rule over you.

And to Adam He said: Because you listened to the voice of your wife, and ate from the tree that I commanded you, saying: You shall not eat from it, cursed is the ground on your account, in toil you shall eat of it all the days of your life.
And it shall grow thorn and thistle for you, and you shall eat the herb of the field.
By the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread, until you return to the ground, for from it you were taken, for you are dust, and to dust you shall return.
And the man called the name of his wife Chavah, for she was the mother of all living.
And Havayah Elokim made for Adam and for his wife tunics of skin, and clothed them.
And Havayah Elokim said: Behold, the man has become as one of us, to know good and evil, and now, lest he send his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever.
And Havayah Elokim sent him from the garden of Eden, to work the ground from which he was taken.
And He drove out the man, and stationed at the east of the garden of Eden the cherubim and the flame of the sword that turns, to guard the way of the tree of life.
And the man knew Chavah his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Kayin, and said: I have acquired a man with Havayah.
And she continued to give birth to his brother, Hevel, and Hevel was a shepherd of flocks, and Kayin was a worker of the ground.
And it was at the end of days, and Kayin brought from the fruit of the ground an offering to Havayah.
And Hevel also brought, from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat, and Havayah turned to Hevel and to his offering.
And to Kayin and to his offering He did not turn, and Kayin was very angry, and his face fell.
And Havayah said to Kayin: Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen?
Is it not, if you do good, you shall be raised up, and if you do not do good, at the entrance sin crouches, and its desire is for you, and you shall rule over it.
And Kayin said to Hevel his brother, and it was, when they were in the field, that Kayin rose against Hevel his brother and killed him.
And Havayah said to Kayin: Where is Hevel your brother? And he said: I do not know, am I my brother's keeper?
And He said: What have you done? The voice of the blood of your brother cries to Me from the ground.
And now, cursed are you from the ground that opened its mouth to take the blood of your brother from your hand.
When you work the ground, it shall not continue to give its strength to you, you shall be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth.
And Kayin said to Havayah: Greater is my punishment than I can bear.

Behold, You have driven me today from upon the face of the ground, and from Your face I shall be hidden, and I shall be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth, and it shall be, anyone who finds me shall kill me.
And Havayah said to him: Therefore, anyone who kills Kayin shall be avenged sevenfold, and Havayah placed for Kayin a sign, so that anyone who finds him shall not strike him.
And Kayin went out from before Havayah, and dwelled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
And Kayin knew his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Chanoch, and he was building a city, and called the name of the city after the name of his son, Chanoch.
And to Chanoch was born Irad, and Irad fathered Mechuyael, and Mechuyael fathered Mesusael, and Mesusael fathered Lemech.
And Lemech took for himself two wives, the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the second was Tzilah.
And Adah gave birth to Yaval, he was the father of those who dwell in tents and of cattle.
And the name of his brother was Yuval, he was the father of all who grasp the harp and the pipe.
And Tzilah also gave birth to Tuval Kayin, a forger of every sharp tool of copper and iron, and the sister of Tuval Kayin was Naamah.
And Lemech said to his wives Adah and Tzilah: Hear my voice, wives of Lemech, listen to my speech, for a man I have killed for my wound, and a child for my bruise.
For sevenfold shall Kayin be avenged, and Lemech seventy-sevenfold.
And Adam knew his wife again, and she gave birth to a son, and called his name Shes, for Elokim has set for me another seed in place of Hevel, for Kayin killed him.
And to Shes also was born a son, and he called his name Enosh, then men began to call upon the name of Havayah.
This is the book of the generations of Adam, on the day Elokim created man, in the likeness of Elokim He made him.
Male and female He created them, and blessed them, and called their name Adam, on the day they were created.
And Adam lived one hundred and thirty years, and fathered a son in his likeness, after his image, and called his name Shes.
And Adam lived after he fathered Shes eight hundred years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Adam were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.
And Shes lived one hundred and five years, and fathered Enosh.
And Shes lived after he fathered Enosh eight hundred and seven years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Shes were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
And Enosh lived ninety years, and fathered Keinan.
And Enosh lived after he fathered Keinan eight hundred and fifteen years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years, and he died.
And Keinan lived seventy years, and fathered Mahalalel.
And Keinan lived after he fathered Mahalalel eight hundred and forty years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Keinan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.
And Mahalalel lived sixty five years, and fathered Yered.
And Mahalalel lived after he fathered Yered eight hundred and thirty years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Mahalalel were eight hundred and ninety five years, and he died.
And Yered lived one hundred and sixty two years, and fathered Chanoch.
And Yered lived after he fathered Chanoch eight hundred years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Yered were nine hundred and sixty two years, and he died.
And Chanoch lived sixty five years, and fathered Mesushelach.
And Chanoch walked with Elokim after he fathered Mesushelach three hundred years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Chanoch were three hundred and sixty-five years.
And Chanoch walked with Elokim, and he was not, for Elokim took him.
And Mesushelach lived one hundred and eighty seven years, and fathered Lemech.
And Mesushelach lived after he fathered Lemech seven hundred and eighty two years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Mesushelach were nine hundred and sixty nine years, and he died.
And Lemech lived one hundred and eighty two years, and fathered a son.
And he called his name Noach, saying: This one shall comfort us from our work and from the toil of our hands, from the ground that Havayah has cursed.
And Lemech lived after he fathered Noach five hundred and ninety five years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Lemech were seven hundred and seventy seven years, and he died.
And Noach was five hundred years old, and Noach fathered Shem, Cham, and Yefet.
And it was when man began to multiply upon the face of the ground, and daughters were born to them.
And the sons of Elokim saw the daughters of man, that they were good, and they took for themselves wives from all that they chose.
And Havayah said: My spirit shall not strive with man forever, for he also is flesh, and his days shall be one hundred and twenty years.

The Nefilim were on the earth in those days, and also after that, when the sons of Elokim would come to the daughters of man, and they bore children to them, they were the mighty men who were from of old, men of renown.
And Havayah saw that the wickedness of man was great on the earth, and every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all the day.
And Havayah regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart.
And Havayah said: I will wipe out man whom I created from upon the face of the ground, from man to beast to creeping thing to bird of the heavens, for I regret that I made them.
And Noach found favor in the eyes of Havayah.
These are the generations of Noach, Noach was a righteous man, perfect in his generations, Noach walked with Elokim.
And Noach fathered three sons, Shem, Cham, and Yefet.
And the earth was corrupted before Elokim, and the earth was filled with violence.
And Elokim saw the earth, and behold, it was corrupted, for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.
And Elokim said to Noach: The end of all flesh has come before Me, for the earth is filled with violence because of them, and behold, I destroy them with the earth.
Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood, you shall make rooms in the ark, and you shall coat it within and without with pitch.
And this is how you shall make it: Three hundred cubits shall be the length of the ark, and fifty cubits its breadth, and thirty cubits its height.
A window you shall make for the ark, and you shall finish it to a cubit above, and you shall place the entrance of the ark in its side, and you shall make it with lower, second, and third stories.
And I, behold, I bring the flood of waters upon the earth to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life from under the heavens, all that is on the earth shall perish.
And I will establish My covenant with you, and you shall come into the ark, you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you.
And from every living thing, from all flesh, two of each you shall bring into the ark to keep alive with you, male and female they shall be.
From the bird after its kind, and from the cattle after its kind, from every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, two of each shall come to you to keep alive.
And you, take for yourself from all food that is eaten, and gather it to you, and it shall be for you and for them for food.
And Noach did according to all that Elokim commanded him, so he did.
And Havayah said to Noach: Come you and all your house into the ark, for you I have seen righteous before Me in this generation.
From every pure animal you shall take for yourself seven, seven, a male and his mate, and from the animal that is not pure, two, a male and his mate.
Also from the bird of the heavens seven, seven, male and female, to keep alive seed upon the face of all the earth.
For in seven more days, I will cause rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe out all existence that I made from upon the face of the ground.
And Noach did according to all that Havayah commanded him.
And Noach was six hundred years old, and the flood was water upon the earth.
And Noach came, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him, into the ark, from before the waters of the flood.
From the pure animal, and from the animal that is not pure, and from the bird, and from every creeping thing that crawls upon the ground.
Two by two they came to Noach into the ark, male and female, as Elokim commanded Noach.
And it was after seven days, and the waters of the flood were upon the earth.

In the six hundredth year of Noach's life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the great deep were broken open, and the windows of the heavens were opened.
And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
On that very day Noach came, and Shem, and Cham, and Yefet, the sons of Noach, and the wife of Noach, and the three wives of his sons with them, into the ark.

They, and every beast after its kind, and every cattle after its kind, and every creeping thing that crawls upon the earth after its kind, and every bird after its kind, every bird, every winged thing.
And they came to Noach into the ark, two by two, from all flesh in which is the breath of life.
And those that came, male and female from all flesh, came as Elokim commanded him, and Havayah closed it for him.
And the flood was forty days upon the earth, and the waters increased, and the ark lifted, and it was raised above the earth.
And the waters grew mighty and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark went upon the face of the waters.
And the waters grew mighty exceedingly upon the earth, and all the high mountains that are under all the heavens were covered that are under all the heavens.
The waters grew fifteen cubits upward, and the mountains were covered.
And all flesh that crawls upon the earth perished, the birds, the cattle, and the beasts, and every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth, and every man.
All in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, from all that was on the dry land, died.

And He wiped out all existence that was upon the face of the ground, from man to cattle to creeping thing to bird of the heavens, and they were wiped out from the earth, and only Noach remained, and those that were with him in the ark.
And the waters were mighty upon the earth one hundred and fifty days.
And Elokim remembered Noach, and all the beasts and all the cattle that were with him in the ark, and Elokim caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.
And the fountains of the deep and the windows of the heavens were stopped, and the rain from the heavens was held back.
And the waters returned from upon the earth, going and returning, and the waters diminished at the end of one hundred and fifty days.
And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
And the waters were going and diminishing until the tenth month, in the tenth month, on the first of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen.
And it was at the end of forty days, and Noach opened the window of the ark that he had made.
And he sent the raven, and it went out, going and returning, until the drying of the waters from upon the earth.
And he sent the dove from him, to see whether the waters had abated from upon the face of the ground.

And the dove did not find rest for the sole of its foot, and it returned to him into the ark, for water was upon the face of all the earth, and he stretched his hand and took it, and brought it to him into the ark.
And he waited yet another seven days, and he sent the dove again from the ark.
And the dove came to him at evening time, and behold, an olive leaf plucked in its mouth, and Noach knew that the waters had abated from upon the earth.
And he waited yet another seven days, and he sent the dove, and it did not return to him again.

And it was in the six hundred and first year, in the first month, on the first of the month, the waters dried from upon the earth, and Noach removed the covering of the ark, and he saw, and behold, the face of the ground was dry.
And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth dried.
And Elokim spoke to Noach, saying:
Go out from the ark, you and your wife and your sons and your sons' wives with you.

Every living thing that is with you, from all flesh, the birds, the cattle, and every creeping thing that crawls upon the earth, bring out with you, and they shall swarm on the earth, and be fruitful and multiply upon the earth.
And Noach went out, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him.
Every beast, every creeping thing, and every bird, everything that crawls upon the earth, after their families, went out from the ark.
And Noach built an altar to Havayah, and took from every pure animal and from every pure bird, and offered burnt offerings upon the altar.

And Havayah smelled the pleasing aroma, and Havayah said in His heart: I will not continue to curse the ground on account of man, for the inclination of the heart of man is evil from his youth, and I will not continue to strike every living thing as I did.
While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.
And Elokim blessed Noach and his sons, and said to them: Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.

And fear of you and dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every bird of the heavens, in all that crawls upon the ground, and in all the fish of the sea, into your hand they are given.
Every creeping thing that lives shall be food for you; as the green herb, I have given you everything.
But flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat.
And your blood, for your lives, I will demand, from the hand of every beast I will demand it, and from the hand of man, from the hand of a man, his brother, I will demand the life of man.
One who sheds the blood of man, by man his blood shall be shed, for in the image of Elokim He made man.
And you, be fruitful and multiply, swarm on the earth, and multiply upon it.
And Elokim said to Noach, and to his sons with him, saying:
And I, behold, I establish My covenant with you, and with your seed after you.
And with every living soul that is with you, in the bird, in the cattle, and in every beast of the earth that is with you, from all that went out of the ark, to every beast of the earth.
And I will establish My covenant with you, and all flesh shall not be cut off again by the waters of the flood, and there shall not be a flood again to destroy the earth.
And Elokim said: This is the sign of the covenant that I place between Me and you and every living soul that is with you, for generations forever.
My bow I have set in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of a covenant between Me and the earth.
And it shall be, when I bring a cloud over the earth, and the bow is seen in the cloud.
And I will remember My covenant that is between Me and you and every living soul of all flesh, and the waters shall not become a flood again to destroy all flesh.
And the bow shall be in the cloud, and I will see it, to remember the everlasting covenant between Elokim and every living soul of all flesh that is upon the earth.
And Elokim said to Noach: This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between Me and all flesh that is upon the earth.
And the sons of Noach who went out of the ark were Shem, and Cham, and Yefet, and Cham was the father of Kena'an.
These three were the sons of Noach, and from these all the earth was spread abroad.
And Noach began, a man of the ground, and planted a vineyard.
And he drank from the wine, and became drunk, and was uncovered within his tent.
And Cham, the father of Kena'an, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brothers outside.

And Shem and Yefet took the garment, and placed it upon the shoulder of both of them, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father, and their faces were backward, and they did not see the nakedness of their father.
And Noach awoke from his wine, and knew what his younger son had done to him.
And he said: Cursed be Kena'an, a servant of servants shall he be to his brothers.
And he said: Blessed be Havayah, the Elokim of Shem, and Kena'an shall be a servant to them.
May Elokim enlarge Yefet, and may He dwell in the tents of Shem, and Kena'an shall be a servant to them.
And Noach lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years.
And all the days of Noach were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.
These are the generations of the sons of Noach, Shem, Cham, and Yefet, and sons were born to them after the flood.
The sons of Yefet: Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Yavan, and Tuval, and Meshech, and Tiras.
And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Rifat, and Togarmah.
And the sons of Yavan: Elishah, and Tarshish, and Kittim, and Dodanim.
From these the isles of the nations were divided in their lands, each after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.
And the sons of Cham: Kush, and Mitzrayim, and Put, and Kena'an.
And the sons of Kush: Seva, and Chavilah, and Savtah, and Raamah, and Savtecha, and the sons of Raamah: Sheva and Dedan.
And Kush fathered Nimrod, he began to be a mighty man on the earth.
He was a mighty hunter before Havayah, therefore it is said: Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before Havayah.
And the beginning of his kingdom was Bavel, and Erech, and Akkad, and Kalneh, in the land of Shinar.
From that land Ashur went out, and built Ninveh, and Rechovos Ir, and Kalach.
And Resen between Ninveh and Kalach, it is the great city.
And Mitzrayim fathered Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehavim, and Naftuchim.
And Patrusim, and Kasluchim, from whom came the Pelishtim, and Kaftorim.
And Kena'an fathered Tzidon his firstborn, and Ches.
And the Yevusi, and the Emori, and the Girgashi.
And the Chivi, and the Arki, and the Sini.
And the Arvadi, and the Tzemari, and the Chamasi, and afterward the families of the Kena'ani were spread abroad.
And the border of the Kena'ani was from Tzidon, as you come to Gerar, until Azzah, as you come to Sedom, and Amorah, and Admah, and Tzevoyim, until Lasha.
These are the sons of Cham, after their families, after their tongues, in their lands, in their nations.
And children were born to Shem also, the father of all the children of Ever, the brother of Yefet the elder.
The sons of Shem: Eilam, and Ashur, and Arpachshad, and Lud, and Aram.
And the sons of Aram: Utz, and Chul, and Geser, and Mash.
And Arpachshad fathered Shelach, and Shelach fathered Ever.
And two sons were born to Ever, the name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided, and the name of his brother was Yoktan.
And Yoktan fathered Almodad, and Shelef, and Chatzarmaves, and Yerach.
And Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah.
And Oval, and Avimael, and Sheva.
And Ofir, and Chavilah, and Yovav, all these were the sons of Yoktan.
And their dwelling was from Mesha, as you come to Sefar, the mountain of the east.
These are the sons of Shem, after their families, after their tongues, in their lands, after their nations.
These are the families of the sons of Noach, after their generations, in their nations, and from these the nations were divided on the earth after the flood.
And all the earth was of one language and of few words.
And it was as they journeyed from the east, and they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they dwelled there.
And they said, each man to his fellow: Come, let us make bricks, and burn them thoroughly, and the brick was for them as stone, and the clay was for them as mortar.
And they said: Come, let us build for ourselves a city, and a tower, and its top in the heavens, and let us make for ourselves a name, lest we be scattered upon the face of all the earth.
And Havayah came down to see the city and the tower that the sons of man built.
And Havayah said: Behold, they are one people, and they all have one language, and this they have begun to do, and now nothing shall be withheld from them of all that they plan to do.
Come, let us go down and confuse their language there, so that a man shall not understand the language of his fellow.
And Havayah scattered them from there upon the face of all the earth, and they ceased to build the city.
Therefore its name was called Bavel, for Havayah confused the language of all the earth there, and from there Havayah scattered them upon the face of all the earth.
These are the generations of Shem, Shem was one hundred years old, and fathered Arpachshad, two years after the flood.
And Shem lived after he fathered Arpachshad five hundred years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And Arpachshad lived thirty five years, and fathered Shelach.
And Arpachshad lived after he fathered Shelach four hundred and three years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And Shelach lived thirty years, and fathered Ever.
And Shelach lived after he fathered Ever four hundred and three years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And Ever lived thirty four years, and fathered Peleg.
And Ever lived after he fathered Peleg four hundred and thirty years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And Peleg lived thirty years, and fathered Reu.
And Peleg lived after he fathered Reu two hundred and nine years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And Reu lived thirty two years, and fathered Serug.
And Reu lived after he fathered Serug two hundred and seven years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And Serug lived thirty years, and fathered Nachor.
And Serug lived after he fathered Nachor two hundred years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And Nachor lived twenty nine years, and fathered Terach.
And Nachor lived after he fathered Terach one hundred and nineteen years, and fathered sons and daughters.
And Terach lived seventy years, and fathered Avram, Nachor, and Charan.
These are the generations of Terach, Terach fathered Avram, Nachor, and Charan, and Charan fathered Lot.
And Charan died before Terach his father, in the land of his birth, in Ur Kasdim.

And Avram and Nachor took wives for themselves, the name of the wife of Avram was Sarai, and the name of the wife of Nachor was Milkah, the daughter of Charan, the father of Milkah and the father of Yiskah.
And Sarai was barren, she had no child.

And Terach took Avram his son, and Lot the son of Charan, the son of his son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of Avram his son, and they went out with them from Ur Kasdim to go to the land of Kena'an, and they came to Charan, and dwelled there.
And the days of Terach were two hundred and five years, and Terach died in Charan.
And Havayah said to Avram: Go for yourself from your land, and from your birthplace, and from the house of your father, to the land that I will show you.
And I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you, and I will make your name great, and you shall be a blessing.
And I will bless those who bless you, and he who curses you I will curse, and all the families of the earth shall be blessed in you.
And Avram went as Havayah spoke to him, and Lot went with him, and Avram was seventy-five years old when he went out from Charan.

And Avram took Sarai his wife, and Lot the son of his brother, and all their wealth that they had acquired, and the souls that they had made in Charan, and they went out to go to the land of Kena'an, and they came to the land of Kena'an.
And Avram passed through the land, until the place of Shechem, until the oak of Moreh, and the Kena'ani was then in the land.
And Havayah appeared to Avram, and said: To your seed I will give this land, and he built there an altar to Havayah, who appeared to him.
And he moved from there to the mountain, east of Beit El, and pitched his tent, Beit El to the west and Ai to the east, and he built there an altar to Havayah, and called upon the name of Havayah.
And Avram journeyed, going and journeying to the south.
And there was a famine in the land, and Avram went down to Mitzrayim to sojourn there, for was severe severe in the land.
And it was when he drew near to come to Mitzrayim, and he said to Sarai his wife: Behold now, I know that you are a beautiful woman.
And it shall be when the Mitzrim see you, and they shall say: This is his wife, and they will kill me, and they will keep you alive.
Please say that you are my sister, so that it will be well with me for your sake, and my soul shall live because of you.
And it was when Avram came to Mitzrayim, and the Mitzrim saw the woman, that she was very beautiful.
And the officers of Paroh saw her, and praised her to Paroh, and the woman was taken to the house of Paroh.
And to Avram he did good for her sake, and he had sheep, and cattle, and donkeys, and servants, and maidservants, and she-donkeys, and camels.
And Havayah afflicted Paroh and his house with great afflictions, because of the matter of Sarai, the wife of Avram.
And Paroh called Avram, and said: What is this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she is your wife?
Why did you say: She is my sister, and I took her to me for a wife, and now, behold your wife, take her and go.
And Paroh commanded men concerning him, and they sent him, and his wife, and all that was his.
And Avram went up from Mitzrayim, he and his wife and all that was his, and Lot with him, to the south.
And Avram was very heavy with cattle, with silver, and with gold.
And he went on his journeys from the south until Beit El, until the place where his tent was at first, between Beit El and Ai.
To the place of the altar that he made there at first, and Avram called there upon the name of Havayah.
And Lot also, who went with Avram, had flocks, and cattle, and tents.
And the land did not bear them to dwell together, for their wealth was great, and they could not dwell together.
And there was strife between the herdsmen of the cattle of Avram and between the herdsmen of the cattle of Lot, and the Kena'ani and the Perizi were then dwelling in the land.
And Avram said to Lot: Please, let there be no strife between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for we are brothers.
Is not all the land before you? Please part from me, if to the left, then I will go to the right, and if to the right, then I will go to the left.

And Lot lifted his eyes, and saw all the plain of the Yarden, that all of it was well watered, before Havayah destroyed Sedom and Amorah, like the garden of Havayah, like the land of Mitzrayim, as you come to Tzoar.
And Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Yarden, and Lot journeyed from the east, and parted each man from his brother.
Avram dwelled in the land of Kena'an, and Lot dwelled in the cities of the plain, and pitched his tent as far as Sedom.
And the men of Sedom were wicked and sinners against Havayah exceedingly.
And Havayah said to Avram, after Lot parted from him: Lift now your eyes, and see from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward.
For all the land that you see, to you I will give it, and to your seed forever.
And I will make your seed as the dust of the earth, so that if a man can count the dust of the earth, also your seed shall be counted.
Arise, walk in the land, in its length and in its breadth, for to you I will give it.
And Avram pitched his tent, and came and dwelled in the plains of Mamre, which are in Chevron, and built there an altar to Havayah.
And it was in the days of Amrafel king of Shinar, Ariokh king of Elasar, Kedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim.
They made war with Bera king of Sedom, and with Birsha king of Amorah, Shinav king of Admah, and Shemever king of Tzevoyim, and the king of Bela, which is Tzoar.
All these joined together to the valley of Sidim, which is the Salt Sea.
Twelve years they served Kedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
And in the fourteenth year Kedorlaomer came, and the kings that were with him, and struck the Refaim in Ashteros Karnayim, and the Zuzim in Cham, and the Eimim in Shaveh Kiryasayim.
And the Chori in their mountain Seir, until Eil Paran, which is by the wilderness.
And they returned, and came to Ein Mishpat, which is Kadesh, and struck all the field of the Amaleki, and also the Emori who dwelled in Chatzatzon Tamar.

And the king of Sedom went out, and the king of Amorah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Tzevoyim, and the king of Bela, which is Tzoar, and they arrayed battle with them in the valley of Sidim.
Against Kedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim, and Amrafel king of Shinar, and Ariokh king of Elasar, four kings against five.
And the valley of Sidim was pits, pits of clay, and the kings of Sedom and Amorah fled, and fell there, and those who remained fled to the mountain.
And they took all the wealth of Sedom and Amorah, and all their food, and went.
And they took Lot, the son of the brother of Avram, and his wealth, and went, and he was dwelling in Sedom.
And the fugitive came, and told Avram the Ivri, and he was dwelling in the plains of Mamre the Emori, the brother of Eshkol, and the brother of Aner, and they were allies of Avram.
And Avram heard that his brother was taken captive, and he armed his trained men, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued as far as Dan.
And he divided himself against them at night, he and his servants, and struck them, and pursued them until Chovah, which is to the left of Damesek.
And he brought back all the wealth, and he brought back also Lot his brother and his wealth, and also the women and the people.
And the king went out of Sedom to meet him, after his return from striking Kedorlaomer and the kings that were with him, to the valley of Shaveh, which is the valley of the king.
And Malki Tzedek king of Shalem brought out bread and wine, and he was a priest of El, the Most High.
And he blessed him, and said: Blessed be Avram to El, the Most High, Master of heaven and earth.
And blessed be El, the Most High, who delivered your enemies into your hand, and he gave him a tenth of everything.
And the king of Sedom said to Avram: Give me the people, and take the wealth for yourself.
And Avram said to the king of Sedom: I have lifted my hand to Havayah, El, the Most High, Master of heaven and earth.
If from a thread to a shoelace, and if I take from all that is yours, then you shall not say: I made Avram rich.
Except only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me, Aner, Eshkol, and Mamre, they shall take their portion.
After these things, the word of Havayah came to Avram in a vision, saying: Fear not, Avram, I am a shield for you, your reward is very great.
And Avram said: Master, Havayah, what will You give me, and I go childless, and the steward of my house is Eliezer of Damesek.
And Avram said: Behold, to me You have not given seed, and behold, a son of my house inherits me.
And behold, the word of Havayah came to him, saying: This one shall not inherit you, but one who comes out from your loins, he shall inherit you.
And He brought him outside, and said: Look now toward the heavens, and count the stars, if you can count them, and He said to him: So your seed shall be.
And he believed in Havayah, and He counted it for him as righteousness.
And He said to him: I am Havayah, who brought you out from Ur Kasdim, to give you this land to inherit it.
And he said: Master, Havayah, how shall I know that I shall inherit it?
And He said to him: Take for Me a heifer of three years, and a she-goat of three years, and a ram of three years, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon.
And he took for Him all these, and divided them in the middle, and placed each half opposite its fellow, and the bird he did not divide.
And the birds of prey descended upon the carcasses, and Avram drove them away.
And it was, the sun was about to set, and a deep sleep fell upon Avram, and behold, a dread, a great darkness, fell upon him.
And He said to Avram: Know for certain that your seed shall be strangers in a land that is not theirs, and they shall serve them, and they shall afflict them four hundred years.
And also the nation that they shall serve, I will judge, and afterward they shall go out with great wealth.
And you shall go to your fathers in peace, you shall be buried in a good old age.
And the fourth generation shall return here, for the iniquity of the Emori is not yet complete until then.
And it was, the sun had set, and thick darkness was, and behold, a smoking furnace and a torch of fire that passed between those pieces.
On that day Havayah cut a covenant with Avram, saying: To your seed I have given this land, from the river of Mitzrayim until the great river, the river Peras.
The Keini, and the Kenizi, and the Kadmoni.
And the Chiti, and the Perizi, and the Refaim.
And the Emori, and the Kena'ani, and the Girgashi, and the Yevusi.
And Sarai, the wife of Avram, had not borne to him, and she had a Mitzri maidservant, and her name was Hagar.
And Sarai said to Avram: Behold now, Havayah has kept me from bearing, come now to my maidservant, perhaps I shall be built up from her, and Avram listened to the voice of Sarai.
And Sarai, the wife of Avram, took Hagar the Mitzri, her maidservant, at the end of ten years of Avram's dwelling in the land of Kena'an, and gave her to Avram her husband for a wife.
And he came to Hagar, and she conceived, and she saw that she had conceived, and her mistress was light in her eyes.
And Sarai said to Avram: My wrong is upon you, I gave my maidservant into your bosom, and she saw that she had conceived, and I was light in her eyes, Havayah shall judge between me and you.
And Avram said to Sarai: Behold, your maidservant is in your hand, do to her what is good in your eyes, and Sarai afflicted her, and she fled from before her.
And the angel of Havayah found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, by the spring on the way to Shur.
And he said: Hagar, maidservant of Sarai, from where have you come, and where are you going? And she said: From Sarai my mistress I flee.
And the angel of Havayah said to her: Return to your mistress, and be afflicted under her hands.
And the angel of Havayah said to her: I will greatly multiply your seed, and it shall not be counted for multitude.
And the angel of Havayah said to her: Behold, you are with child, and you shall bear a son, and you shall call his name Yishmael, for Havayah has heard your affliction.
And he shall be a wild man, his hand against everyone, and the hand of everyone against him, and before all his brothers he shall dwell.
And she called the name of Havayah, who spoke to her: You are El of seeing, for she said: Have I also seen here after seeing?
Therefore the well was called Be'er Lachai Roi, behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
And Hagar bore to Avram a son, and Avram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Yishmael.
And Avram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Yishmael to Avram.
And Avram was ninety-nine years old, and Havayah appeared to Avram, and said to him: I am El Shaddai, walk before Me, and be wholehearted.
And I will give My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly, exceedingly.
And Avram fell upon his face, and Elokim spoke with him, saying:
As for Me, behold, My covenant is with you, and you shall be a father of a multitude of nations.
And your name shall no more be called Avram, and your name shall be Avraham, for a father of a multitude of nations I have made you.
And I will make you fruitful exceedingly, exceedingly, and I will make you into nations, and kings shall come out from you.
And I will establish My covenant between Me and you, and your seed after you in their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be for you for Elokim, and for your seed after you.
And I will give to you and to your seed after you the land of your sojournings, all the land of Kena'an, for an everlasting possession, and I will be for them for Elokim.
And Elokim said to Avraham: And you shall keep My covenant, you, and your seed after you in their generations.
This is My covenant that you shall keep, between Me and you and your seed after you: Every male among you shall be circumcised.
And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of a covenant between Me and you.
And a son of eight days shall be circumcised among you, every male in your generations, one born in the house, and one bought with silver from any foreigner who is not of your seed.
One born in your house and one bought with your silver shall surely be circumcised, and My covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant. for an everlasting covenant.
And an uncircumcised male, who shall not circumcise the flesh of his foreskin, and that soul shall be cut off from its people, My covenant he has broken.
And Elokim said to Avraham: Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, for Sarah is her name.
And I will bless her, and also I will give you from her a son, and I will bless her, and she shall become nations, kings of peoples shall come from her.
And Avraham fell upon his face, and laughed, and said in his heart: Shall one who is one hundred years old have a child born, and shall Sarah, a woman of ninety years, give birth?
And Avraham said to Elokim: If only Yishmael might live before You.
And Elokim said: Indeed, Sarah your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Yitzchak, and I will establish My covenant with him for an everlasting covenant, for his seed after him.

And as for Yishmael, I have heard you, behold, I have blessed him, and I will make him fruitful, and I will multiply him exceedingly, exceedingly, twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him into a great nation.
And My covenant I will establish with Yitzchak, whom Sarah shall bear to you at this appointed time, in the next year.
And He finished speaking with him, and Elokim went up from upon Avraham.

And Avraham took Yishmael his son, and all those born in his house, and all those bought with his silver, every male among the men of the house of Avraham, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin on that very day, as Elokim spoke with him.
And Avraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
And Yishmael his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
On that very day Avraham was circumcised, and Yishmael his son.
And all the men of his house, born in the house, and bought with silver from a foreigner, were circumcised with him.
And Havayah appeared to him in the plains of Mamre, and he was sitting at the entrance of the tent in the heat of the day.
And he lifted his eyes and saw, and behold, three men were standing before him, and he saw them, and ran to meet them from the entrance of the tent, and bowed himself to the ground.
And he said: My Master, if now I have found favor in Your eyes, please do not pass from Your servant.
Please let a little water be taken, and wash your feet, and recline under the tree.
And I will take a morsel of bread, and sustain your hearts, and afterward you shall pass on, for therefore you have passed by your servant, and they said: Do so, as you have said.
And Avraham hurried to the tent, to Sarah, and said: Hurry, three measures of fine flour, knead, and make cakes.
And Avraham ran to the cattle, and took a calf, tender and good, and gave it to the lad, and he hurried to prepare it.
And he took butter and milk, and the calf that he had prepared, and set it before them, and he stood over them under the tree, and they ate.
And they said to him: Where is Sarah your wife? And he said: Behold, in the tent.
And he said: I will surely return to you at this time next year, and behold, Sarah your wife shall have a son, and Sarah was listening at the entrance of the tent, and it was behind him.
And Avraham and Sarah were old, advanced in days, the way of women had ceased to be with Sarah.
And Sarah laughed within herself, saying: After I have withered, shall I have pleasure, and my lord is old?
And Havayah said to Avraham: Why did Sarah laugh, saying: Shall I indeed bear, and I am old?
Is anything too wondrous for Havayah? At the appointed time I will return to you, at this time next year, and Sarah shall have a son.
And Sarah denied, saying: I did not laugh, for she was afraid, and He said: No, but you did laugh.
And the men rose from there, and looked toward Sedom, and Avraham went with them to escort them.
And Havayah said: Shall I hide from Avraham what I am doing?
And Avraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him.

For I have known him, so that he shall command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of Havayah, to do righteousness and justice, so that Havayah will bring upon Avraham that which He spoke concerning him.
And Havayah said: The cry of Sedom and Amorah, for it is great, and their sin, for it is very heavy.
I will go down now, and see whether according to its cry that has come to Me they have done, utterly, and if not, I will know.
And the men turned from there, and went to Sedom, and Avraham was still standing before Havayah.
And Avraham drew near, and said: Will You sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
Perhaps there are fifty righteous within the city, will You sweep away, and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous who are within it?
Far be it from You to do such a thing, to kill the righteous with the wicked, and the righteous shall be as the wicked, far be it from You, shall the Judge of all the earth not do justice?
And Havayah said: If I find in Sedom fifty righteous within the city, I will spare the whole place for their sake.
And Avraham answered, and said: Behold now, I have presumed to speak to my Master, and I am dust and ashes.
Perhaps the fifty righteous shall lack five, will You destroy for five the whole city? And He said: I will not destroy, if I find there forty-five.
And he continued to speak to Him, and said: Perhaps forty shall be found there, and He said: I will not do it for the sake of the forty.
And he said: Please let my Master not be angry, and I will speak, perhaps thirty shall be found there, and He said: I will not do it, if I find there thirty.
And he said: Behold now, I have presumed to speak to my Master, perhaps twenty shall be found there, and He said: I will not destroy for the sake of the twenty.
And he said: Please let my Master not be angry, and I will speak only this once, perhaps ten shall be found there, and He said: I will not destroy for the sake of the ten.
And Havayah went, when He finished speaking to Avraham, and Avraham returned to his place.
And the two angels came to Sedom in the evening, and Lot was sitting at the gate of Sedom, and Lot saw, and rose to meet them, and bowed himself with his face to the earth.

And he said: Behold now, my masters, please turn aside to the house of your servant, and lodge, and wash your feet, and you shall rise early and go on your way, and they said: No, for in the street we will lodge.
And he urged them greatly, and they turned aside to him, and came into his house, and he made them a feast, and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
Before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sedom, surrounded the house, from young to old, all the people from every quarter.
And they called Lot, and said to him: Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, and we will know them.
And Lot went out to them to the entrance, and closed the door behind him.
And he said: Please, my brothers, do not do evil.

Behold now, I have two daughters who have not known a man, I will bring them out to you, and do to them as is good in your eyes, only to these men do nothing, for therefore they have come under the shadow of my roof.

And they said: Stand back, and they said: This one came to sojourn, and now he would judge us, now we will do worse to you than to them, and they pressed hard upon the man, upon Lot, and drew near to break the door.
And the men stretched out their hand, and brought Lot to them into the house, and closed the door.
And they struck the men who were at the entrance of the house with blindness, from small to great, and they wearied themselves to find the entrance.
And the men said to Lot: Whom else do you have here? A son-in-law, and your sons, and your daughters, and all that you have in the city, bring out from the place.
For we are destroying this place, for their cry is great before Havayah, and Havayah has sent us to destroy it.

And Lot went out, and spoke to his sons-in-law, who had taken his daughters, and said: Arise, go out from this place, for Havayah is destroying the city, and he seemed as one who jests in the eyes of his sons-in-law.
And when the dawn rose, the angels urged Lot, saying: Arise, take your wife and your two daughters who are found here, lest you be swept away in the iniquity of the city.

And he lingered, and the men took hold of his hand, and of the hand of his wife, and of the hand of his two daughters, in the mercy of Havayah upon him, and they brought him out, and set him outside the city.
And it was, when they brought them out, that he said: Flee for your life, do not look behind you, and do not stand in all the plain, flee to the mountain, lest you be swept away.
And Lot said to them: Please, no, my masters.

Behold now, your servant has found favor in your eyes, and you have magnified your kindness that you have done with me, to save my life, and I cannot flee to the mountain, lest the evil overtake me, and I die.
Behold now, this city is near to flee there, and it is small, please let me flee there, is it not small, and my soul shall live?
And he said to him: Behold, I have lifted your face for this thing also, not to overturn the city of which you have spoken.
Hurry, flee there, for I cannot do anything until you come there, therefore the name of the city was called Tzoar.
The sun rose upon the earth, and Lot came to Tzoar.
And Havayah rained brimstone and fire upon Sedom and upon Amorah, from Havayah, from the heavens.
And He overturned those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and the growth of the ground.
And his wife looked behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
And Avraham rose early in the morning, to the place where he had stood before Havayah.
And he looked toward Sedom and Amorah, and toward all the land of the plain, and saw, and behold, the smoke of the land went up, like the smoke of a furnace.
And it was, when Elokim destroyed the cities of the plain, that Elokim remembered Avraham, and sent Lot out from the midst of the overturning, when He overturned the cities in which Lot had dwelled.
And Lot went up from Tzoar, and dwelled in the mountain, and his two daughters with him, for he feared to dwell in Tzoar, and he dwelled in a cave, he and his two daughters.
And the elder said to the younger: Our father is old, and there is no man on the earth to come to us as is the way of all the earth.
Come, let us make our father drink wine, and lie with him, and we shall keep alive seed from our father.
And they made their father drink wine that night, and the elder came and lay with her father, and he did not know when she lay down, and when she arose.

And it was on the next day, and the elder said to the younger: Behold, I lay last night with my father, let us make him drink wine tonight also, and you go and lie with him, and we shall keep alive seed from our father.
And they made their father drink wine that night also, and the younger arose and lay with him, and he did not know when she lay down, and when she arose.
And the two daughters of Lot conceived from their father.
And the elder bore a son, and called his name Moav, he is the father of Moav to this day.
And the younger also bore a son, and called his name Ben Ami, he is the father of the children of Ammon to this day.
And Avraham journeyed from there to the land of the south, and dwelled between Kadesh and Shur, and sojourned in Gerar.
And Avraham said of Sarah his wife: She is my sister, and Avimelech, king of Gerar, sent, and took Sarah.
And Elokim came to Avimelech in a dream of the night, and said to him: Behold, you are a dead man, because of the woman that you have taken, and she is married to a husband.
And Avimelech had not come near her, and he said: Master, will You kill a nation, even a righteous one?
Did he not say to me: She is my sister, and she, she also said: He is my brother, in the innocence of my heart and in the cleanness of my hands I have done this.
And Elokim said to him in the dream: I too know that in the innocence of your heart you did this, and I too kept you from sinning against Me, therefore I did not let you touch her.
And now, return the wife of the man, for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for you, and you shall live, and if you do not return her, know that you shall surely die, you and all that is yours.
And Avimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and spoke all these words in their ears, and the men were very afraid.

And Avimelech called Avraham, and said to him: What have you done to us, and what have I sinned against you, that you have brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin? Deeds that should not be done, you have done to me.
And Avimelech said to Avraham: What did you see, that you did this thing?
And Avraham said: Because I said: Surely there is no fear of Elokim in this place, and they will kill me over the matter of my wife.
And also, truly, she is my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife.

And it was, when Elokim caused me to wander from the house of my father, that I said to her: This is your kindness that you shall do with me, at every place where we shall come, say of me: He is my brother.
And Avimelech took flocks and cattle, and servants and maidservants, and gave them to Avraham, and returned to him Sarah his wife.
And Avimelech said: Behold, my land is before you, where it is good in your eyes, dwell.
And to Sarah he said: Behold, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver, behold, it is for you a covering of the eyes for all who are with you, and with all, you are vindicated.
And Avraham prayed to Elokim, and Elokim healed Avimelech, and his wife, and his maidservants, and they bore children.
For Havayah closed up every womb of the house of Avimelech, because of Sarah, the wife of Avraham.
And Havayah remembered Sarah, as He had said, and Havayah did for Sarah as He had spoken.
And Sarah conceived, and bore a son to Avraham in his old age, at the appointed time that Elokim spoke to him.
And Avraham called the name of his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Yitzchak.
And Avraham circumcised Yitzchak his son, a son of eight days, as Elokim commanded him.
And Avraham was one hundred years old when Yitzchak his son was born to him.
And Sarah said: Elokim has made laughter for me, everyone who hears will laugh for me.
And she said: Who would have said to Avraham that Sarah would nurse children, for I have borne a son in his old age.
And the child grew, and was weaned, and Avraham made a great feast on the day Yitzchak was weaned.
And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Mitzri, whom she bore to Avraham, playing.
And she said to Avraham: Drive out this maidservant and her son, for the son of this maidservant shall not inherit with my son, with Yitzchak.
And the matter was very evil in the eyes of Avraham, concerning his son.

And Elokim said to Avraham: Let it not be evil in your eyes concerning the lad and concerning your maidservant, all that Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, for in Yitzchak seed shall be called for you.
And the son of the maidservant also I will make into a nation, for your seed is he.

And Avraham rose early in the morning, and took bread and a skin of water, and gave them to Hagar, placing them upon her shoulder, and the child, and sent her away, and she went, and wandered in the wilderness of Be'er Sheva.
And the water from the skin was finished, and she cast the child under one of the bushes.
And she went, and sat herself down opposite, far off, about a bowshot away, for she said: Let me not see the death of the child, and she sat opposite, and lifted her voice, and wept.
And Elokim heard the voice of the lad, and the angel of Elokim called Hagar from the heavens, and said to her: What ails you, Hagar? Fear not, for Elokim has heard the voice of the lad, where he is.
Arise, lift up the lad, and hold him with your hand, for into a great nation I will make him.
And Elokim opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water, and she went, and filled the skin with water, and gave the lad to drink.
And Elokim was with the lad, and he grew, and dwelled in the wilderness, and became an archer.
And he dwelled in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Mitzrayim.
And it was at that time, and Avimelech and Pichol, the chief of his host, said to Avraham, saying: Elokim is with you in all that you do.

And now, swear to me by Elokim here, that you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my son's son, according to the kindness that I have done with you, you shall do with me, and with the land in which you have sojourned.
And Avraham said: I will swear.
And Avraham reproved Avimelech concerning the well of water that the servants of Avimelech had seized.
And Avimelech said: I do not know who did this thing, and you also did not tell me, nor have I heard, except today.
And Avraham took flocks and cattle, and gave to Avimelech, and the two of them cut a covenant.
And Avraham set the seven ewe-lambs of the flock by themselves.
And Avimelech said to Avraham: What are these seven ewe-lambs that you have set by themselves?
And he said: For the seven ewe-lambs you shall take from my hand, so that it shall be a testimony for me, that I dug this well.
Therefore he called that place Be'er Sheva, for there the two of them swore.
And they cut a covenant in Be'er Sheva, and Avimelech and Pichol, the chief of his host, rose, and they returned to the land of the Pelishtim.
And he planted a tamarisk in Be'er Sheva, and called there upon the name of Havayah, El of the world.
And Avraham sojourned in the land of the Pelishtim many days.
And it was after these things, and Elokim tested Avraham, and He said to him: Avraham, and he said: Here I am.
And He said: Take now your son, your only one, whom you love, Yitzchak, and go to the land of Moriyah, and offer him up there as a burnt offering upon one of the mountains that I will tell you.

And Avraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his donkey, and took two of his young men with him, and Yitzchak his son, and split the wood for the burnt offering, and rose, and went to the place that Elokim told him.
On the third day Avraham lifted his eyes, and saw the place from afar.
And Avraham said to his young men: Stay here with the donkey, and I and the lad will go yonder, and we will bow down, and return to you.
And Avraham took the wood of the burnt offering, and placed it upon Yitzchak his son, and took in his hand the fire and the knife, and the two of them went together.
And Yitzchak spoke to Avraham his father, and said: My father, and he said: Here I am, my son, and he said: Behold, the fire and the wood, and where is the lamb for a burnt offering?
And Avraham said: Elokim will see for Himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son, and the two of them went together.
And they came to the place that Elokim told him, and Avraham built the altar there, and arranged the wood, and bound Yitzchak his son, and placed him on the altar, upon the wood.
And Avraham stretched out his hand, and took the knife to slaughter his son.
And the angel of Havayah called him from the heavens, and said: Avraham, Avraham, and he said: Here I am.
And he said: Do not stretch out your hand to the lad, and do not do to him anything, for now I know that you fear Elokim, and you did not withhold your son, your only one, from Me.
And Avraham lifted his eyes, and saw, and behold, a ram behind him, caught in the thicket by its horns, and Avraham went, and took the ram, and offered it up as a burnt offering instead of his son.
And Avraham called the name of that place Havayah Yireh, as it is said to this day: On the mountain Havayah will be seen.
And the angel of Havayah called Avraham a second time from the heavens.
And he said: By Myself I have sworn, Havayah says, for because you have done this thing, and did not withhold your son, your only one.
I will surely bless you, and I will surely multiply your seed, as the stars of the heavens and as the sand that is upon the shore of the sea, and your seed shall inherit the gate of his enemies.
And all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in your seed, because you listened to My voice.
And Avraham returned to his young men, and they rose, and went together to Be'er Sheva, and Avraham dwelled in Be'er Sheva.
And it was after these things, and it was told to Avraham, saying: Behold, Milkah has borne children also to Nachor your brother.
Utz his firstborn, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram.
And Kesed, and Chazo, and Pildash, and Yidlaf, and Besuel.
And Besuel fathered Rivkah, these eight bore Milkah to Nachor, the brother of Avraham.
And his concubine, and her name was Reumah, she also bore Tevach, and Gacham, and Tachash, and Maachah.
And Sarah's life was one hundred years, and twenty years, and seven years, the years of Sarah's life.
And Sarah died in Kiryas Arba, which is Chevron, in the land of Kena'an, and Avraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her.
And Avraham rose from before his dead, and spoke to the children of Ches, saying:
I am a stranger and a resident with you, give me a burial holding with you, and I will bury my dead from before me.
And the children of Ches answered Avraham, saying to him:
Hear us, my master, you are a prince of Elokim in our midst, in the choicest of our graves bury your dead, none of us shall withhold his grave from you, from burying your dead.
And Avraham rose, and bowed himself before the people of the land, before the children of Ches.
And he spoke with them, saying: If it is your will to bury my dead from before me, hear me, and entreat for me to Efron, the son of Tzochar.
That he may give me the cave of Machpelah, which is his, which is at the end of his field, for full silver shall he give it to me in your midst, for a burial holding.
And Efron was sitting among the children of Ches, and Efron answered the Chiti Avraham in the hearing of the children of Ches, of all who came to the gate of his city, saying:
No, my master, hear me, the field I have given you, and the cave that is in it, I have given you, before the eyes of the sons of my people I have given it to you, bury your dead.
And Avraham bowed himself before the people of the land.
And he spoke to Efron in the hearing of the people of the land, saying: But if you will only hear me, I have given the silver for the field, take it from me, and I will bury my dead there.
And Efron answered Avraham, saying to him:
My master, hear me, land worth four hundred shekels of silver, between me and you, what is it? And bury your dead.
And Avraham listened to Efron, and Avraham weighed the silver to Efron that he spoke in the hearing of the children of Ches, four hundred shekels of silver, passing with the merchant.

And the field of Efron was established, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, and the cave that was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, that were within all its border around.
For Avraham as a possession, before the eyes of the children of Ches, of all who came to the gate of his city.
And after that, Avraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah, before Mamre, which is Chevron, in the land of Kena'an.
And the field was established, and the cave that was in it, for Avraham as a burial holding, from the children of Ches.
And Avraham was old, advanced in days, and Havayah blessed Avraham with everything.
And Avraham said to his servant, the elder of his house, who ruled over all that he had: Please place your hand under my thigh.
And I will make you swear by Havayah, Elokim of the heavens and Elokim of the earth, that you shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Kena'ani, among whom I dwell.
But to my land and to my birthplace you shall go, and take a wife for my son, for Yitzchak.
And the servant said to him: Perhaps the woman will not wish to follow me to this land, shall I bring back your son to the land from which you came out?
And Avraham said to him: Beware, lest you bring my son back there.

Havayah, Elokim of the heavens, who took me from the house of my father and from my birthplace, and who spoke to me, and swore to me, saying: To your seed I will give this land, He will send His angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
And if the woman will not wish to follow you, then you shall be clear from this oath of mine, only you shall not bring my son back there.
And the servant placed his hand under the thigh of Avraham his master, and swore to him concerning this matter.
And the servant took ten camels from the camels of his master, and went, and all the good of his master was in his hand, and he arose, and went to Aram Naharayim, to the city of Nachor.
And he made the camels kneel outside the city by the well of water, at evening time, the time when the women who draw water go out.
And he said: Havayah, Elokim of my master Avraham, please grant success before me today, and do kindness with my master Avraham.
Behold, I stand by the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water.

And it shall be, the young woman to whom I shall say: Tilt your jug, please, that I may drink, and she shall say: Drink, and also your camels I will give to drink, You have confirmed her for Your servant, for Yitzchak, and through her I shall know that You have done kindness with my master.
And it was, before he finished speaking, and behold, Rivkah came out, who was born to Besuel, the son of Milkah, the wife of Nachor, the brother of Avraham, and her jug was upon her shoulder.
And the young woman was very good to look upon, a virgin, and no man had known her, and she went down to the spring, and filled her jug, and came up.
And the servant ran toward her, and said: Please let me sip a little water from your jug.
And she said: Drink, my master, and she hurried, and lowered her jug upon her hand, and gave him to drink.
And she finished giving him to drink, and said: Also for your camels I will draw, until they finish drinking.
And she hurried, and emptied her jug into the trough, and ran again to the well to draw, and drew for all his camels.
And the man gazed at her in wonder, keeping silent, to know whether Havayah had made his journey successful or not.
And it was, when the camels finished drinking, that the man took a gold ring, weighing half a shekel, and two bracelets upon her hands, weighing ten shekels of gold.
And he said: Whose daughter are you? Please tell me, is there room in the house of your father for us to lodge?
And she said to him: I am the daughter of Besuel, the son of Milkah, whom she bore to Nachor.
And she said to him: Also straw and feed are plentiful with us, also room to lodge.
And the man bowed, and prostrated himself to Havayah.

And he said: Blessed be Havayah, Elokim of my master Avraham, who has not withheld His kindness and His truth from my master, and as for me, Havayah has guided me on the way, to the house of my master's brothers.
And the young woman ran, and told the household of her mother these things.
And Rivkah had a brother, and his name was Lavan, and Lavan ran out to the man, to the spring.

And it was, when he saw the ring and the bracelets upon the hands of his sister, and when he heard the words of Rivkah his sister, saying: So the man spoke to me, that he came to the man, and behold, he was standing by the camels at the spring.
And he said: Come, blessed of Havayah, why do you stand outside, for I have cleared the house, and a place for the camels.
And the man came into the house, and he unloaded the camels, and gave straw and feed for the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the feet of the men who were with him.
And food was set before him to eat, and he said: I will not eat until I have spoken my words, and he said: Speak.
And he said: I am the servant of Avraham.
And Havayah has blessed my master greatly, and he has become great, and He gave him flocks and cattle, and silver and gold, and servants and maidservants, and camels and donkeys.
And Sarah, the wife of my master, bore a son to my master after her old age, and he gave to him all that he has.
And my master made me swear, saying: You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Kena'ani, in whose land I dwell.
But to the house of my father you shall go, and to my family, and take a wife for my son.
And I said to my master: Perhaps the woman will not follow me.

And he said to me: Havayah, before whom I have walked, will send His angel with you, and make your way successful, and you shall take a wife for my son from my family, and from the house of my father.
Then you shall be clear from my oath, when you come to my family, and if they do not give to you, then you shall be clear from my oath.
And I came today to the spring, and I said: Havayah, Elokim of my master Avraham, if You would please make successful the way upon which I go.
Behold, I stand by the spring of water, and it shall be, the young woman who comes out to draw, and I say to her: Please give me a little water to drink from your jug.
And she says to me: You too drink, and for your camels also I will draw, she is the woman whom Havayah has confirmed for the son of my master.
I, before I finished speaking in my heart, and behold, Rivkah came out, and her jug was upon her shoulder, and she went down to the spring, and drew, and I said to her: Please give me to drink.
And she hurried, and lowered her jug from upon her, and said: Drink, and your camels also I will give to drink, and I drank, and the camels also she gave to drink.

And I asked her, and said: Whose daughter are you? And she said: The daughter of Besuel, the son of Nachor, whom Milkah bore to him, and I placed the ring upon her nose, and the bracelets upon her hands.
And I bowed, and prostrated myself to Havayah, and I blessed Havayah, Elokim of my master Avraham, who guided me on the way of truth, to take the daughter of my master's brother for his son.
And now, if you will do kindness and truth with my master, tell me, and if not, tell me, and I will turn to the right or to the left.
And Lavan and Besuel answered, and said: The matter has come out from Havayah, we cannot speak to you bad or good.
Behold, Rivkah is before you, take her and go, and she shall be a wife for the son of your master, as Havayah has spoken.
And it was, when the servant of Avraham heard their words, that he prostrated himself to the earth to Havayah.
And the servant brought out vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and gave to Rivkah, and precious things he gave to her brother and to her mother.
And they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and they lodged, and they rose in the morning, and he said: Send me to my master.
And her brother and her mother said: Let the young woman stay with us some days, or ten months, afterward she shall go.
And he said to them: Do not delay me, for Havayah has made my way successful, send me, and I will go to my master.
