And they said: We will call the young woman, and ask her.
And they called Rivkah, and said to her: Will you go with this man? And she said: I will go.
And they sent Rivkah their sister, and her nurse, and the servant of Avraham, and his men.
And they blessed Rivkah, and said to her: Our sister, may you become thousands of myriads, and may your seed inherit the gate of those who hate them.
And Rivkah rose, and her young women, and they rode upon the camels, and went after the man, and the servant took Rivkah, and went.
And Yitzchak came from the way to Be'er Lachai Roi, and he was dwelling in the land of the south.
And Yitzchak went out to meditate in the field toward evening, and he lifted his eyes, and saw, and behold, camels were coming.
And Rivkah lifted her eyes, and saw Yitzchak, and she fell from the camel.
And she said to the servant: Who is that man who walks in the field toward us? And the servant said: He is my master, and she took the veil, and covered herself.
And the servant told Yitzchak all the things that he had done.
And Yitzchak brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother, and he took Rivkah, and she became his wife, and he loved her, and Yitzchak was comforted after his mother.
And Avraham added and took a wife, and her name was Keturah.
And she bore to him Zimran, and Yokshan, and Medan, and Midyan, and Yishbak, and Shuah.
And Yokshan begot Sheva and Dedan, and the sons of Dedan were Ashurim, and Letushim, and Le'umim.
And the sons of Midyan were Ephah, and Efer, and Hanokh, and Avida, and Eldaah, all these were the children of Keturah.
And Avraham gave all that he had to Yitzchak.
And to the sons of the concubines that Avraham had, Avraham gave gifts, and sent them away from Yitzchak his son, while he was still alive, eastward, to the east country.
And these are the days of the years of Avraham's life, which he lived: one hundred years, and seventy years, and five years.
And Avraham expired, and died at a good old age, aged and content, and was gathered to his people.
And Yitzchak and Yishmael his sons buried him in the Cave of Makhpelah, in the field of Efron, the son of Tzochar the Chiti, which is before Mamre.
The field that Avraham purchased from the children of Het, there Avraham was buried, and Sarah his wife.
And it was, after the death of Avraham, that Elokim blessed Yitzchak his son, and Yitzchak dwelt beside Be'er Lachai Roi.
And these are the generations of Yishmael, the son of Avraham, whom Hagar the Mitzri, the maidservant of Sarah, bore to Avraham.
And these are the names of the sons of Yishmael, by their names, according to their birth: the firstborn of Yishmael, Nevayos, and Kedar, and Adbe'el, and Mivsam.
Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa.
Hadad, and Temah, Yetur, Nafish, and Kedem.
These are the sons of Yishmael, and these are their names, by their encampments, and by their fortified towns, twelve princes according to their nations.
And these are the years of Yishmael's life: one hundred years, and thirty years, and seven years, and he expired, and died, and was gathered to his people.
And they dwelt from Chavilah until Shur, which is before Mitzrayim, as you go toward Ashur, before all his brothers he settled.
And these are the generations of Yitzchak, the son of Avraham: Avraham begot Yitzchak.
And Yitzchak was forty years old when he took Rivkah, the daughter of Besuel the Arami, from Padan Aram, the sister of Lavan the Arami, to him for a wife.
And Yitzchak entreated Havayah on behalf of his wife, because she was barren, and Havayah was entreated by him, and Rivkah his wife conceived.
And the children struggled within her, and she said: If so, why am I thus? And she went to inquire of Havayah.

And Havayah said to her: Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be separated from your innards, and one people shall be stronger than the other people, and the elder shall serve the younger.
And her days were fulfilled to give birth, and behold, twins were in her womb.
And the first came out red, all of him like a cloak of hair, and they called his name Esav.
And after that came out his brother, and his hand grasped the heel of Esav, and he called his name Yackov, and Yitzchak was sixty years old when she bore them.
And the lads grew, and Esav was a man who knew hunting, a man of the field, and Yackov was a wholehearted man, dwelling in tents.
And Yitzchak loved Esav, because game was in his mouth, and Rivkah loved Yackov.
And Yackov cooked a stew, and Esav came from the field, and he was weary.
And Esav said to Yackov: Feed me, please, from this red thing, for I am weary, therefore his name was called Edom.
And Yackov said: Sell me today your birthright.
And Esav said: Behold, I am going to die, and what is this birthright to me?
And Yackov said: Swear to me today, and he swore to him, and sold his birthright to Yackov.
And Yackov gave to Esav bread and a stew of lentils, and he ate and drank, and arose and went, and Esav scorned the birthright.
And there was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Avraham, and Yitzchak went to Avimelech, king of the Pelishtim, to Gerar.
And Havayah appeared to him, and said: Do not go down to Mitzrayim, dwell in the land that I will tell you.
Reside in this land, and I will be with you, and I will bless you, for to you and to your seed I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath that I swore to Avraham your father.
And I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens, and I will give to your seed all these lands, and all the nations of the earth shall bless themselves through your seed.
Because Avraham listened to My voice, and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My teachings.
And Yitzchak dwelt in Gerar.

And the men of the place asked about his wife, and he said: She is my sister, for he feared to say: She is my wife, lest the men of the place kill me on account of Rivkah, because she is good to look upon.
And it was, when the days were prolonged to him there, that Avimelech, king of the Pelishtim, looked out through the window, and saw, and behold, Yitzchak was laughing with Rivkah his wife.
And Avimelech called Yitzchak, and said: Behold, she is indeed your wife, and how did you say: She is my sister? And Yitzchak said to him: Because I said: Lest I die on account of her.
And Avimelech said: What is this that you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.
And Avimelech commanded all the people, saying: Whoever touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.
And Yitzchak sowed in that land, and found in that year a hundredfold, and Havayah blessed him.
And the man grew great, and went on, growing greater and greater, until he became very great.
And he had flocks of sheep, and herds of cattle, and a great household, and the Pelishtim envied him.
And all the wells that the servants of his father had dug in the days of Avraham his father, the Pelishtim stopped them up, and filled them with earth.
And Avimelech said to Yitzchak: Go from us, for you have become much mightier than we.
And Yitzchak went from there, and encamped in the valley of Gerar, and dwelt there.

And Yitzchak returned and dug the wells of water that they had dug in the days of Avraham his father, and the Pelishtim stopped them up after the death of Avraham, and he called them by names like the names that his father called them.
And the servants of Yitzchak dug in the valley, and found there a well of living water.
And the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with the herdsmen of Yitzchak, saying: Ours is the water, and he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.
And they dug another well, and they quarreled over it also, and he called its name Sitnah.
And he moved from there, and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it, and he called its name Rechovos, and said: For now Havayah has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.
And he went up from there to Be'er Sheva.

And Havayah appeared to him on that night, and said: I am the Elokim of Avraham your father, do not fear, for I am with you, and I will bless you, and multiply your seed, for the sake of Avraham My servant.
And he built an altar there, and called upon the name of Havayah, and pitched his tent there, and the servants of Yitzchak dug a well there.
And Avimelech went to him from Gerar, with Achuzas his friend and Pichol the captain of his army.
And Yitzchak said to them: Why have you come to me, and you hated me, and sent me away from you?
And they said: We have surely seen that Havayah is with you, and we said: Let there be an oath between us, between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you.
That you will do us no harm, as we have not touched you, and as we have done with you only good, and sent you away in peace, you are now the blessed of Havayah.
And he made for them a feast, and they ate and drank.
And they rose early in the morning, and swore each to his brother, and Yitzchak sent them away, and they went from him in peace.
And it was on that day, that the servants of Yitzchak came and told him about the well that they had dug, and said to him: We have found water.
And he called it Shivah, therefore the name of the city is Be'er Sheva to this day.
And Esav was forty years old, and he took as wife Yehudis, the daughter of Be'eri the Chiti, and Basmas, the daughter of Eilon the Chiti.
And they were a bitterness of spirit to Yitzchak and to Rivkah.
And it was, when Yitzchak was old, and his eyes were dim from seeing, and he called Esav his elder son, and said to him: My son, and he said to him: Here I am.
And he said: Behold, I have grown old, I do not know the day of my death.
And now, please take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field, and hunt game for me.
And make for me tasty food, as I love, and bring it to me, and I will eat, so that my soul may bless you before I die.
And Rivkah heard as Yitzchak spoke to Esav his son, and Esav went to the field to hunt game to bring.
And Rivkah said to Yackov her son, saying: Behold, I heard your father speak to Esav your brother, saying:
Bring me game, and make for me tasty food, and I will eat, and bless you before Havayah before my death.
And now, my son, heed my voice to that which I command you.
Go now to the flock, and take for me from there two fine goat kids, and I will make them tasty food for your father, as he loves.
And you shall bring it to your father, and he shall eat, so that he will bless you before his death.
And Yackov said to Rivkah his mother: Behold, Esav my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.
Perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall be in his eyes as a deceiver, and I shall bring upon myself a curse and not a blessing.
And his mother said to him: Upon me be your curse, my son, only heed my voice, and go, take them for me.
And he went, and took them, and brought them to his mother, and his mother made tasty food, as his father loved.
And Rivkah took the fine garments of Esav her elder son, which were with her in the house, and she dressed her younger son Yackov in them.
And the skins of the goat kids she placed upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck.
And she gave the tasty food and the bread that she had made into the hand of Yackov her son.
And he came to his father, and said: My father, and he said: Here I am, who are you, my son?
And Yackov said to his father: I am Esav your firstborn, I have done as you spoke to me, arise now, sit and eat from my game, so that your soul may bless me.
And Yitzchak said to his son: How is it that you found so quickly, my son? And he said: Because Havayah your Elokim made it happen before me.
And Yitzchak said to Yackov: Approach now, that I may feel you, my son, whether you are my son Esav or not.
And Yackov approached Yitzchak his father, and he felt him, and said: The voice is the voice of Yackov, and the hands are the hands of Esav.
And he did not recognize him, for his hands were hairy like the hands of Esav his brother, and he blessed him.
And he said: Are you my son Esav? And he said: I am.
And he said: Bring it near to me, and I will eat from my son's game, so that my soul may bless you, and he brought it near to him, and he ate, and he brought him wine, and he drank.
And Yitzchak his father said to him: Approach now, and kiss me, my son.
And he approached, and kissed him, and he smelled the scent of his garments, and blessed him, and said: See, the scent of my son is as the scent of a field that Havayah has blessed.
And may Elokim give you from the dew of the heavens, and from the fatness of the earth, and abundance of grain and wine.

Peoples shall serve you, and nations shall bow down to you, be a master to your brothers, and your mother's sons shall bow down to you, cursed be those who curse you, and blessed be those who bless you.
And it was, when Yitzchak finished blessing Yackov, and Yackov had just gone out from before Yitzchak his father, that Esav came his brother from his hunt.
And he too made tasty food, and brought it to his father, and said to his father: Let my father arise, and eat from his son's game, so that your soul may bless me.
And Yitzchak his father said to him: Who are you? And he said: I am your son, your firstborn, Esav.
And Yitzchak trembled with a very great trembling, and said: Who then is the one who hunted game and brought it to me, and I ate from all before you came, and blessed him? He shall also be blessed.
When Esav heard the words of his father, he cried out a great and bitter cry, and said to his father: Bless me too, my father.
And he said: Your brother came with cunning, and took your blessing.

And he said: Is it because his name was called Yackov, that he has deceived me these two times? He took my birthright, and behold, now he has taken my blessing, and he said: Have you not reserved a blessing for me?

And Yitzchak answered and said to Esav: Behold, I have made him a master to you, and I have given all his brothers to him as servants, and with grain and wine I have sustained him, and for you then, what shall I do, my son?
And Esav said to his father: Have you but one blessing, my father? Bless me too, my father, and Esav raised his voice and wept.
And Yitzchak answered his father and said to him: Behold, your dwelling shall be from the fatness of the earth, and from the dew of the heavens above.
By your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother, and it shall be, when you revolt, that you shall break his yoke from upon your neck.
And Esav hated Yackov because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him, and Esav said in his heart: The days of mourning for my father will approach, and I will kill Yackov my brother.
And the words of Esav her elder son were told to Rivkah, and she sent and called Yackov her younger son, and said to him: Behold, Esav your brother consoles himself concerning you, to kill you.
And now, my son, heed my voice, and arise, flee to Lavan my brother, to Charan.
And dwell with him a few days, until the anger of your brother turns away.
Until the anger of your brother turns away from you, and he forgets what you did to him, and I will send and take you from there, why should I be bereaved of both of you in one day?
And Rivkah said to Yitzchak: I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Het, if Yackov takes a wife from the daughters of Het, like these, from the daughters of the land, why do I need life?
And Yitzchak called Yackov, and blessed him, and commanded him, and said to him: Do not take a wife from the daughters of Kena'an.
Arise, go to Padan Aram, to the house of Besuel, the father of your mother, and take for yourself from there a wife, from the daughters of Lavan, the brother of your mother.
And El Shaddai will bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, and you shall be an assembly of peoples.
And may He give you the blessing of Avraham, to you and to your seed with you, to inherit the land of your sojourning, which Elokim gave to Avraham.
And Yitzchak sent Yackov, and he went to Padan Aram, to Lavan, the son of Besuel the Arami, the brother of Rivkah, the mother of Yackov and Esav.

And Esav saw that Yitzchak blessed Yackov, and sent him to Padan Aram, to take for himself from there a wife, in blessing him, he commanded him, saying: Do not take a wife from the daughters of Kena'an.
And Yackov heeded his father and his mother, and went to Padan Aram.
And Esav saw that the daughters of Kena'an were evil in the eyes of Yitzchak his father.
And Esav went to Yishmael, and took Machalas, the daughter of Yishmael, the son of Avraham, the sister of Nevayos, in addition to his wives, to him for a wife.
And Yackov went out from Be'er Sheva, and went to Charan.
And he encountered the place, and lodged there, because the sun had set, and he took from the stones of the place, and placed them at his head, and lay down in that place.
And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder set upon the earth, and its top reached the heavens, and behold, the angels of Elokim were ascending and descending upon it.
And behold, Havayah stood upon him, and said: I am Havayah, the Elokim of Avraham your father, and the Elokim of Yitzchak, the land upon which you lie, to you I will give it, and to your seed.

And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and you shall spread out westward, and eastward, and northward, and southward, and shall be blessed through you all the families of the earth, and through your seed.
And behold, I am with you, and I will guard you wherever you go, and bring you back to this land, for I will not leave you until I have done that which I have spoken to you.
And Yackov awoke from his sleep, and said: Surely Havayah is in this place, and I did not know.
And he was afraid, and said: How awesome is this place, this is none other than the house of Elokim, and this is the gate of the heavens.
And Yackov rose early in the morning, and took the stone that he had placed at his head, and set it up as a monument, and poured oil upon its top.
And he called the name of that place Beit El, but Luz was the name of the city at first.
And Yackov vowed a vow, saying: If Elokim will be with me, and guard me on this way that I go, and give me bread to eat and a garment to wear.
And I return to my father's house in peace, then Havayah shall be my Elokim.
And this stone that I have set up as a monument shall be the house of Elokim, and of all that You give me, I will surely tithe it to You.
And Yackov lifted his feet, and went to the land of the people of the east.

And he saw, and behold, a well in the field, and behold, there were three flocks of sheep lying beside it, for from that well they watered the flocks, and the stone upon the mouth of the well was great.
And all the flocks would gather there, and they would roll the stone from the mouth of the well, and water the sheep, and return the stone upon the mouth of the well to its place.
And Yackov said to them: My brothers, from where are you? And they said: We are from Charan.
And he said to them: Do you know Lavan, the son of Nachor? And they said: We know him.
And he said to them: Is he well? And they said: He is well, and behold, Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep.
And he said: Behold, the day is still great, it is not time to gather the livestock, water the sheep, and go, pasture them.
And they said: We cannot, until all the flocks are gathered, and they roll the stone from the mouth of the well, and we water the sheep.
While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with the flock of her father, for she was a shepherdess.

And it was, when Yackov saw Rachel, the daughter of Lavan, the brother of his mother, and the flock of Lavan, the brother of his mother, that Yackov approached, and rolled the stone from the mouth of the well, and watered the flock of Lavan, the brother of his mother.
And Yackov kissed Rachel, and raised his voice, and wept.
And Yackov told Rachel that he was her father's brother, and that he was the son of Rivkah, and she ran and told her father.
And it was, when Lavan heard the report of Yackov, the son of his sister, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house, and he told Lavan all these things.
And Lavan said to him: Surely you are my bone and my flesh, and he dwelt with him a month's time.
And Lavan said to Yackov: Because you are my brother, shall you serve me for nothing? Tell me, what is your wage?
And Lavan had two daughters, the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
And the eyes of Leah were tender, and Rachel was beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance.
And Yackov loved Rachel, and said: I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter.
And Lavan said: It is better that I give her to you than that I give her to another man, dwell with me.
And Yackov served seven years for Rachel, and they were in his eyes as a few days, in his love for her.
And Yackov said to Lavan: Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, and I will come to her.
And Lavan gathered all the men of the place, and made a feast.
And it was in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him, and he came to her.
And Lavan gave to her Zilpah his maidservant, to Leah his daughter, as a maidservant.
And it was in the morning, and behold, she was Leah, and he said to Lavan: What is this that you have done to me? Did I not serve you for Rachel, and why have you deceived me?
And Lavan said: It is not done so in our place, to give the younger before the elder.
Complete the week of this one, and we will give you this one also, for the service that you shall serve with me yet another seven years.
And Yackov did so, and completed the week of this one, and he gave him Rachel his daughter for a wife.
And Lavan gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his maidservant, to her as a maidservant.
And he came also to Rachel, and loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet another seven years.
And Havayah saw that Leah was hated, and opened her womb, and Rachel was barren.
And Leah conceived, and bore a son, and called his name Reuven, for she said: Because Havayah has seen my affliction, for now my husband will love me.
And she conceived again, and bore a son, and said: Because Havayah has heard that I am hated, and He has given me this one also, and she called his name Shimon.
And she conceived again, and bore a son, and said: Now this time my husband will be joined to me, for I have borne him three sons, therefore he called his name Levi.
And she conceived again, and bore a son, and said: This time I will give thanks to Havayah, therefore she called his name Yehudah, and she ceased bearing.
And Rachel saw that she did not bear to Yackov, and Rachel envied her sister, and said to Yackov: Give me children, and if not, I am dead.
And the anger of Yackov burned against Rachel, and he said: Am I in the place of Elokim, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?
And she said: Behold, my maidservant Bilhah, come to her, and she shall bear upon my knees, and I too shall be built up through her.
And she gave him Bilhah her maidservant as a wife, and Yackov came to her.
And Bilhah conceived, and bore a son to Yackov.
And Rachel said: Elokim has judged me, and has also heard my voice, and has given me a son, therefore she called his name Dan.
And Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, conceived again, and bore a second son to Yackov.
And Rachel said: With wrestlings of Elokim I have wrestled with my sister, and I have also prevailed, and she called his name Naftali.
And Leah saw that she had ceased bearing, and she took Zilpah her maidservant, and gave her to Yackov as a wife.
And Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, bore a son to Yackov.
And Leah said: Good fortune has come, and she called his name Gad.
And Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, bore a second son to Yackov.
And Leah said: In my happiness, for the daughters will call me happy, and she called his name Asher.
And Reuven went in the days of the wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to Leah his mother, and Rachel said to Leah: Please give me from your son's mandrakes.

And she said to her: Is it a small thing that you have taken my husband, and to take also my son's mandrakes? And Rachel said: Therefore he shall lie with you tonight, in exchange for your son's mandrakes.
And Yackov came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said: To me you shall come, for I have hired you with my son's mandrakes, and he lay with her that night.
And Elokim heeded Leah, and she conceived, and bore a fifth son to Yackov.
And Leah said: Elokim has given my reward, because I gave my maidservant to my husband, and she called his name Yissachar.
And Leah conceived again, and bore a sixth son to Yackov.
And Leah said: Elokim has endowed me with a good endowment, this time my husband will dwell with me, for I have borne him six sons, and she called his name Zevulun.
And afterward she bore a daughter, and called her name Dinah.
And Elokim remembered Rachel, and Elokim heeded her, and opened her womb.
And she conceived, and bore a son, and said: Elokim has taken away my disgrace.
And she called his name Yosef, saying: May Havayah add to me another son.
And it was, when Rachel bore Yosef, that Yackov said to Lavan: Send me away, and I will go to my place, and to my land.
Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, and I will go, for you know my service that I served you.
And Lavan said to him: If now I have found favor in your eyes, I have divined, and Havayah has blessed me on your account.
And he said: Specify your wages for me, and I will give it.
And he said to him: You know how I served you, and how your livestock was with me.
For the little that you had before me has increased greatly, and Havayah has blessed you with my coming, and now, when shall I provide also for my own house?
And he said: What shall I give you? And Yackov said: You shall give me nothing, if you will do this thing for me, I will return, I will pasture your flock, I will guard it.

I will pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted lamb, and every brown lamb among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats, and it shall be my wages.

And my righteousness shall answer for me on the coming day, when you come over my wages before you, every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and brown among the sheep, is stolen with me.
And Lavan said: Behold, would that it be according to your word.

And he removed on that day the he-goats that were streaked and spotted, and all the she-goats that were speckled and spotted, every one that had white in it, and all the brown among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons.
And he set a journey of three days between himself and Yackov, and Yackov pastured the rest of the flock of Lavan.
And Yackov took for himself rods of fresh poplar, and almond, and plane, and peeled in them white peelings, exposing the white that was in the rods.
And he set the rods that he had peeled in the troughs, in the watering places of the water, where the flock came to drink, facing the flock, and they came into heat when they came to drink.
And the flocks came into heat at the rods, and the flocks bore streaked, speckled, and spotted.

And Yackov separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flock toward the streaked and all the brown in the flock of Lavan, and he set for himself droves alone, and did not set them with the flock of Lavan.
And it was, whenever the strong flocks came into heat, that Yackov set the rods before the eyes of the flock in the troughs, to bring them into heat by the rods.
And when the flocks were feeble, he did not set them, and the feeble were Lavan's, and the strong were Yackov's.
And the man increased exceedingly, and he had many flocks, and maidservants and servants, and camels and donkeys.
And he heard the words of the sons of Lavan, saying: Yackov has taken all that was our father's, and from that which was our father's he has made all this wealth.
And Yackov saw the face of Lavan, and behold, it was not with him as yesterday and the day before.
And Havayah said to Yackov: Return to the land of your fathers, and to your birthplace, and I will be with you.
And Yackov sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field, to his flock.
And he said to them: I see the face of your father, that it is not toward me as yesterday and the day before, and the Elokim of my father has been with me.
And you know that with all my strength I have served your father.
And your father has deceived me, and changed my wages ten times, and Elokim did not allow him to harm me.
If he said: The speckled shall be your wages, then all the flock bore speckled, and if he said: The streaked shall be your wages, then all the flock bore streaked.
And Elokim has taken away the livestock of your father, and has given it to me.
And it was, at the time the flock came into heat, that I lifted my eyes, and saw in a dream, and behold, the he-goats that mounted the flock were streaked, speckled, and mottled.
And the angel of Elokim said to me in the dream: Yackov, and I said: Here I am.
And he said: Lift your eyes now, and see, all the he-goats that mount the flock are streaked, speckled, and mottled, for I have seen all that Lavan does to you.
I am the El of Beit El, where you anointed a monument, where you vowed to Me a vow, now arise, go out from this land, and return to the land of your birth.
And Rachel and Leah answered and said to him: Is there still for us a portion and an inheritance in the house of our father?
Are we not reckoned by him as strangers, for he has sold us, and has also consumed our silver?
For all the wealth that Elokim has taken from our father, it is ours and our children's, and now, all that Elokim has said to you, do.
And Yackov arose, and set his sons and his wives upon the camels.
And he led all his livestock, and all his property that he had acquired, the livestock of his acquisition that he had acquired in Padan Aram, to come to Yitzchak his father, to the land of Kena'an.
And Lavan had gone to shear his sheep, and Rachel stole the teraphim that were her father's.
And Yackov stole the heart of Lavan the Arami, for he did not tell him that he was fleeing.
And he fled, he and all that he had, and arose, and crossed the river, and set his face toward Mount Gilad.
And it was told to Lavan on the third day that Yackov had fled.
And he took his brothers with him, and pursued after him a journey of seven days, and overtook him in Mount Gilad.
And Elokim came to Lavan the Arami in a dream of the night, and said to him: Beware, lest you speak to Yackov from good to bad.
And Lavan overtook Yackov, and Yackov had pitched his tent in the mountain, and Lavan pitched with his brothers in Mount Gilad.
And Lavan said to Yackov: What have you done, that you stole my heart, and led my daughters as captives of the sword?
Why did you flee in secret, and steal my heart, and not tell me, that I might have sent you with joy and with songs, with drum and with harp?
And you did not let me kiss my sons and my daughters, now you have acted foolishly.
There is power in my hand to do you harm, but the Elokim of your father spoke to me last night, saying: Beware, lest you speak to Yackov from good to bad.
And now, you have gone, because you longed for your father's house, why did you steal my gods?
And Yackov answered and said to Lavan: Because I feared, for I said: Lest you take your daughters from me.
With whomever you find your gods, he shall not live, before our brothers, discern what is with me, and take it for yourself, and Yackov did not know that Rachel had stolen them.

And Lavan came into the tent of Yackov, and into the tent of Leah, and into the tent of the two maidservants, and did not find them, and he went out from the tent of Leah, and came into the tent of Rachel.
And Rachel had taken the teraphim, and put them in the camel's saddle, and sat upon them, and Lavan felt all the tent, and did not find them.
And she said to her father: Let it not be angry in the eyes of my lord, that I cannot rise before you, for the way of women is upon me, and he searched, and did not find the teraphim.
And Yackov was angry, and quarreled with Lavan, and Yackov answered and said to Lavan: What is my transgression, what is my sin, that you have pursued after me?
For you have felt all my vessels, what have you found of all the vessels of your house? Put it here before my brothers and your brothers, and let them judge between the two of us.
These twenty years I have been with you, your ewes and your she-goats did not miscarry, and the rams of your flock I did not eat.
That which was torn I did not bring to you, I bore the loss of it, from my hand you demanded it, stolen by day and stolen by night.
By day the heat consumed me, and the frost by night, and my sleep fled from my eyes.
These are twenty years for me in your house, I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you changed my wages ten times.

Had the Elokim of my father, the Elokim of Avraham, and the Fear of Yitzchak, not been with me, you would now have sent me away empty, Elokim saw my affliction and the toil of my hands, and reproved you last night.

And Lavan answered and said to Yackov: The daughters are my daughters, and the sons are my sons, and the flock is my flock, and all that you see is mine, and to my daughters, what shall I do to them today, or to their sons whom they have borne?
And now, come, let us make a covenant, I and you, and it shall be a witness between me and you.
And Yackov took a stone, and set it up as a monument.
And Yackov said to his brothers: Gather stones, and they took stones, and made a heap, and they ate there upon the heap.
And Lavan called it Yegar Sahaduta, and Yackov called it Gal'ed.
And Lavan said: This heap is a witness between me and you today, therefore he called its name Gal'ed.
And the Mitzpah, for he said: May Havayah watch between me and you, when we are hidden one from another.
If you afflict my daughters, and if you take wives in addition to my daughters, no man is with us, see, Elokim is witness between me and you.
And Lavan said to Yackov: Behold, this heap, and behold, the monument that I have set between me and you.
This heap is a witness, and the monument is a witness, that I will not pass to you this heap, and that you shall not pass to me this heap and this monument, for harm.
The Elokim of Avraham, and the Elokim of Nachor, the Elokim of their father, shall judge between us, and Yackov swore by the Fear of his father Yitzchak.
And Yackov offered a sacrifice on the mountain, and called his brothers to eat bread, and they ate bread, and lodged on the mountain.
And Lavan rose early in the morning, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them, and Lavan went and returned to his place.
And Yackov went on his way, and angels of Elokim encountered him.
And Yackov said when he saw them: This is the camp of Elokim, and he called the name of that place Machanayim.
And Yackov sent messengers before him to Esav his brother, to the land of Seir, the field of Edom.
And he commanded them, saying: So shall you say to my lord, to Esav: So says your servant Yackov: With Lavan I have sojourned, and I have tarried until now.
And I have oxen, and donkeys, flocks, and menservants and maidservants, and I have sent to tell my lord, to find favor in your eyes.
And the messengers returned to Yackov, saying: We came to your brother, to Esav, and also he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him.
And Yackov was afraid very much, and he was distressed, and he divided the people who were with him, and the flocks, and the cattle, and the camels, into two camps.
And he said: If Esav comes to the one camp, and smites it, then the remaining camp shall escape.
And Yackov said: Elokim of my father Avraham, and Elokim of my father Yitzchak, Havayah, who said to me: Return to your land, and to your birthplace, and I will do good with you.
I am unworthy of all the kindnesses, and of all the truth, that You have done with Your servant, for with my staff I crossed this Yarden, and now I have become two camps.
Deliver me, please, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esav, for I fear him, lest he come and smite me, mother with children.
And You said: I will surely do good with you, and make your seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.
And he lodged there that night, and took from what came into his hand a gift for Esav his brother.
Two hundred she-goats, and twenty he-goats, two hundred ewes, and twenty rams.
Thirty nursing camels and their young, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty she-donkeys and ten he-donkeys.
And he gave them into the hand of his servants, each drove by itself, and said to his servants: Pass before me, and put a space between drove and drove.
And he commanded the first, saying: When Esav my brother meets you, and asks you, saying: Whose are you, and where are you going, and whose are these before you?
Then you shall say: Your servant Yackov's, a gift it is sent to my lord, to Esav, and behold, he too is behind us.
And he commanded also the second, also the third, also all who went after the droves, saying: According to this word shall you speak to Esav, when you find him.

And you shall say: Moreover, behold, your servant Yackov is behind us, for he said: I will appease his face with the gift that goes before me, and afterward I will see his face, perhaps he will lift my face.
And the gift passed before him, and he lodged that night in the camp.
And he arose in that night, and took his two wives, and his two maidservants, and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of the Yabok.
And he took them, and brought them over the stream, and brought over that which he had.
And Yackov was left alone, and a man wrestled with him until the breaking of the dawn.
And he saw that he could not prevail against him, and he touched the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Yackov's thigh was strained, as he wrestled with him.
And he said: Let me go, for the dawn has risen, and he said: I will not let you go, unless you bless me.
And he said to him: What is your name? And he said: Yackov.
And he said: Your name shall no longer be called Yackov, but Yisroel, for you have striven with Elokim and with men, and have prevailed.
And Yackov asked, and said: Tell me, please, your name, and he said: Why is it that you ask my name? And he blessed him there.
And Yackov called the name of the place Peniel, for I have seen Elokim face to face, and my soul was saved.
And the sun rose for him as he passed Penuel, and he was limping upon his thigh.
Therefore the children of Yisroel do not eat the sinew of the hip, which is upon the hollow of the thigh, to this day, because he touched the hollow of Yackov's thigh, in the sinew of the hip.
And Yackov lifted his eyes, and saw, and behold, Esav came, and with him four hundred men, and he divided the children among Leah, and Rachel, and the two maidservants.
And he put the maidservants and their children first, and Leah and her children after them, and Rachel and Yosef last.
And he passed before them, and bowed to the earth seven times, until he approached his brother.
And Esav ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell upon his neck, and kissed him, and they wept.
And he lifted his eyes, and saw the women and the children, and said: Who are these to you? And he said: The children with whom has Elokim favored your servant.
And the maidservants approached, they and their children, and bowed down.
And Leah also approached, and her children, and bowed down, and afterward Yosef and Rachel approached, and bowed down.
And he said: What is to you all this camp that I met? And he said: To find favor in the eyes of my lord.
And Esav said: I have much, my brother, let what is yours be yours.
And Yackov said: Please, no, if now I have found favor in your eyes, then take my gift from my hand, for therefore I have seen your face, as one sees the face of Elokim, and you have favored me.
Please take my blessing that was brought to you, for Elokim has favored me, and for I have everything, and he pressed him, and he took it.
And he said: Let us journey, and let us go, and I will go before you.
And he said to him: My lord knows that the children are tender, and the flocks and the cattle that are nursing are upon me, and if they drive them one day, then all the flocks will die.

Please let my lord pass before his servant, and I will lead on slowly, according to the pace of the work that is before me, and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my lord, to Seir.
And Esav said: Let me now leave with you some of the people who are with me, and he said: Why is this? Let me find favor in the eyes of my lord.
And Esav returned on that day on his way to Seir.
And Yackov journeyed to Sukkos, and built him a house, and made booths for his livestock, therefore he called the name of the place Sukkos.
And Yackov came whole to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Kena'an, when he came from Padan Aram, and encamped before the city.
And he bought the portion of the field, where he had pitched his tent, from the hand of the children of Chamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred kesitah.
And he set up there an altar, and called it El, Elokim of Yisroel.
And Dinah went out, the daughter of Leah, whom she bore to Yackov, to see the daughters of the land.
And Shechem, the son of Chamor the Chivi, the prince of the land, saw her, and took her, and lay with her, and afflicted her.
And his soul clung to Dinah, the daughter of Yackov, and he loved the young woman, and spoke to the heart of the young woman.
And Shechem said to Chamor his father, saying: Take for me this girl as a wife.
And Yackov heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter, and his sons were with his livestock in the field, and Yackov was silent until they came.
And Chamor went out, the father of Shechem, to Yackov to speak with him.

And the sons of Yackov came from the field when they heard it, and the men were grieved, and they were very angry, because he had done a disgraceful thing in Yisroel, to lie with the daughter of Yackov, and so it shall not be done.
And Chamor spoke with them, saying: The soul of Shechem my son longs for your daughter, please give her to him as a wife.
And intermarry with us, give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for you.
And you shall dwell with us, and the land shall be before you, dwell and trade in it, and settle in it.
And Shechem said to her father and to her brothers: Let me find favor in your eyes, and what you say to me I will give.
Multiply upon me exceedingly the bride-price and gift, and I will give as you say to me, and give me the young woman as a wife.
And the sons of Yackov answered Shechem and Chamor his father with deceit, and spoke, because he had defiled Dinah their sister.
And they said to them: We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to a man who has a foreskin, for it is a disgrace to us.
Only with this will we consent to you, if you become as we are, to circumcise every male among you.
And we will give our daughters to you, and your daughters we will take for us, and we will dwell with you, and become one people.
And if you will not listen to us, to be circumcised, then we will take our daughter, and go.
And their words were good in the eyes of Chamor, and in the eyes of Shechem, the son of Chamor.
And the lad did not delay to do the thing, for he desired the daughter of Yackov, and he was honored above all the house of his father.
And Chamor and Shechem his son came to the gate of their city, and spoke to the men of their city, saying:

These men are at peace with us, and they shall dwell in the land, and trade in it, and behold, the land is broad before them, their daughters we will take to us as wives, and our daughters we will give to them.
Only with this will the men consent to us, to dwell with us, to become one people, when every male among us is circumcised, as they are circumcised.
Their livestock, and their property, and all their cattle, shall they not be ours? Only let us consent to them, and they will dwell with us.
And all who went out of the gate of his city listened to Chamor and to Shechem his son, and every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.

And it was on the third day, when they were in pain, that the two sons of Yackov, Shimon and Levi, the brothers of Dinah, took each his sword, and came upon the city confidently, and killed every male.
And they killed Chamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and they took Dinah from the house of Shechem, and went out.
The sons of Yackov came upon the slain, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.
They took their flocks, and their cattle, and their donkeys, and that which was in the city, and that which was in the field.
And they took captive all their wealth, and all their little ones, and their wives, and plundered all that was in the house.

And Yackov said to Shimon and to Levi: You have troubled me, to make me loathsome to the inhabitants of the land, to the Kena'ani and to the Perizi, and I am few in number, and they will gather against me, and smite me, and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.
And they said: Shall he make our sister as a harlot?
And Elokim said to Yackov: Arise, go up to Beit El, and dwell there, and make there an altar to the El who appeared to you when you fled from Esav your brother.
And Yackov said to his household, and to all who were with him: Remove the foreign gods that are among you, and purify yourselves, and change your garments.
And we will arise, and go up to Beit El, and I will make there an altar to the El who answered me on the day of my distress, and was with me on the way that I went.
And they gave to Yackov all the foreign gods that were in their hand, and the rings that were in their ears, and Yackov hid them under the terebinth that is by Shechem.
And they journeyed, and the terror of Elokim was upon the cities that were around them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Yackov.
And Yackov came to Luz, which is in the land of Kena'an, that is Beit El, he and all the people who were with him.
And he built there an altar, and he called the place El Beit El, because there the Elokim were revealed to him, when he fled from his brother.
And Devorah, the nurse of Rivkah, died, and she was buried below Beit El, under the oak, and he called its name Alon Bachus.
And Elokim appeared to Yackov again, when he came from Padan Aram, and He blessed him.
And Elokim said to him: Your name is Yackov, your name shall no longer be called Yackov, but Yisroel shall be your name, and He called his name Yisroel.
And Elokim said to him: I am El Shaddai, be fruitful and multiply, a nation and an assembly of nations shall be from you, and kings shall come out of your loins.
And the land that I gave to Avraham and to Yitzchak, to you I will give it, and to your seed after you I will give the land.
And Elokim went up from him, in the place where He spoke with him.
And Yackov set up a monument in the place where He spoke with him, a monument of stone, and he poured upon it a libation, and poured oil upon it.
And Yackov called the name of the place where Elokim spoke with him Beit El.
And they journeyed from Beit El, and there was still a distance of land to come to Efras, and Rachel was in labor, and she had difficulty in her labor.
And it was, when she had difficulty in her labor, that the midwife said to her: Do not fear, for this too is a son for you.
And it was, when her soul was departing, for she was dying, that she called his name Ben Oni, and his father called him Binyamin.
And Rachel died, and she was buried on the way to Efras, that is Beit Lechem.
And Yackov set up a monument upon her grave, that is the monument of the grave of Rachel to this day.
And Yisroel journeyed, and pitched his tent beyond Migdal Eder.
And it was, when Yisroel dwelt in that land, that Reuven went and lay with Bilhah, the concubine of his father, and Yisroel heard, and the sons of Yackov were twelve.
The sons of Leah: Reuven, the firstborn of Yackov, and Shimon, and Levi, and Yehudah, and Yissachar, and Zevulun.
The sons of Rachel: Yosef and Binyamin.
And the sons of Bilhah, the maidservant of Rachel: Dan and Naftali.
And the sons of Zilpah, the maidservant of Leah: Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Yackov, who were born to him in Padan Aram.
And Yackov came to Yitzchak his father, to Mamre, to Kiryas Arba, that is Chevron, where Avraham and Yitzchak sojourned.
And the days of Yitzchak were one hundred years and eighty years.
And Yitzchak expired, and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days, and Esav and Yackov his sons buried him.
These are the generations of Esav, he is Edom.
Esav took his wives from the daughters of Kena'an: Adah, the daughter of Eilon the Chiti, and Oholivama, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Tzivon the Chivi.
And Basmas, the daughter of Yishmael, the sister of Nevayos.
And Adah bore Elifaz to Esav, and Basmas bore Reuel.
And Oholivama bore Yeush, and Ya'elam, and Korach, these are the sons of Esav, who were born to him in the land of Kena'an.

And Esav took his wives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the souls of his house, and his livestock, and all his cattle, and all his property that he had acquired in the land of Kena'an, and went to a land, away from Yackov his brother.
For their property was too great for them to dwell together, and the land of their sojourning could not bear them, because of their livestock.
And Esav dwelt on Mount Seir, Esav, he is Edom.
And these are the generations of Esav, the father of Edom, on Mount Seir.
These are the names of the sons of Esav: Elifaz, the son of Adah, the wife of Esav, Reuel, the son of Basmas, the wife of Esav.
And the sons of Elifaz were Teman, Omar, Tzefo, and Gatam, and Kenaz.
And Timna was a concubine of Elifaz, the son of Esav, and she bore to Elifaz Amalek, these are the sons of Adah, the wife of Esav.
And these are the sons of Reuel: Nachas, and Zerach, Shammah, and Mizzah, these were the sons of Basmas, the wife of Esav.
And these were the sons of Oholivama, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Tzivon, the wife of Esav, and she bore to Esav Yeush, and Ya'elam, and Korach.
These are the chiefs of the sons of Esav: the sons of Elifaz, the firstborn of Esav: the chief of Teman, the chief of Omar, the chief of Tzefo, the chief of Kenaz.
The chief of Korach, the chief of Gatam, the chief of Amalek, these are the chiefs of Elifaz in the land of Edom, these are the sons of Adah.

And these are the sons of Reuel, the son of Esav: the chief of Nachas, the chief of Zerach, the chief of Shammah, the chief of Mizzah, these are the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom, these are the sons of Basmas, the wife of Esav.
And these are the sons of Oholivama, the wife of Esav: the chief of Yeush, the chief of Ya'elam, the chief of Korach, these are the chiefs of Oholivama, the daughter of Anah, the wife of Esav.
These are the sons of Esav, and these are their chiefs, he is Edom.
These are the sons of Seir the Chori, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, and Shoval, and Tzivon, and Anah.
And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan, these are the chiefs of the Chorim, the sons of Seir, in the land of Edom.
And the sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam, and the sister of Lotan was Timna.
And these are the sons of Shoval: Alvan, and Manachas, and Eval, Shefo, and Onam.
And these are the sons of Tzivon: Ayah and Anah, he is Anah who found the Yemim in the wilderness, when he pastured the donkeys of Tzivon his father.
And these are the sons of Anah: Dishon, and Oholivama, the daughter of Anah.
And these are the sons of Dishon: Hemdan, and Eshban, and Yisran, and Keran.
These are the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Akan.
These are the sons of Dishan: Utz and Aran.
These are the chiefs of the Chorim: the chief of Lotan, the chief of Shoval, the chief of Tzivon, the chief of Anah.
The chief of Dishon, the chief of Ezer, the chief of Dishan, these are the chiefs of the Chorim, according to their chiefs in the land of Seir.
And these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before a king reigned for the children of Yisroel.
And Bela, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhavah.
And Bela died, and Yovav, the son of Zerach, from Botzrah, reigned in his stead.
And Yovav died, and Husham, from the land of the Temanim, reigned in his stead.
And Husham died, and Hadad, the son of Bedad, who smote Midyan in the field of Moav, reigned in his stead, and the name of his city was Avis.
And Hadad died, and Samlah, from Masrekah, reigned in his stead.
And Samlah died, and Shaul, from Rechovos on the river, reigned in his stead.
And Shaul died, and Baal Chanan, the son of Achbor, reigned in his stead.
And Baal Chanan, the son of Achbor, died, and Hadar reigned in his stead, and the name of his city was Pau, and the name of his wife was Mehetavel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mei Zahav.
And these are the names of the chiefs of Esav, according to their families, according to their places, by their names: the chief of Timna, the chief of Alvah, the chief of Yetet.
The chief of Oholivama, the chief of Elah, the chief of Pinon.
The chief of Kenaz, the chief of Teman, the chief of Mivtzar.
The chief of Magdiel, the chief of Iram, these are the chiefs of Edom, according to their dwellings in the land of their possession, he is Esav, the father of Edom.
And Yackov dwelt in the land of the sojournings of his father, in the land of Kena'an.

These are the generations of Yackov: Yosef, seventeen years old, was herding the flock with his brothers, and he was a lad with the sons of Bilhah and with the sons of Zilpah, the wives of his father, and Yosef brought an evil report of them to their father.
And Yisroel loved Yosef more than all his sons, for he was a son of his old age to him, and he made him a fine tunic.
And his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, and they hated him, and they could not speak peaceably to him.
And Yosef dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brothers, and they hated him even more.
And he said to them: Please hear this dream that I dreamed.
Behold, we were binding sheaves in the midst of the field, and behold, my sheaf arose and also stood upright, and behold, your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to my sheaf.
And his brothers said to him: Will you surely reign over us? Will you surely rule over us? And they hated him even more for his dreams and for his words.
And he dreamed yet another dream, and he told it to his brothers, and he said: Behold, I dreamed another dream, and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.

And he told it to his father and to his brothers, and his father rebuked him, and said to him: What is this dream that you dreamed? Shall we come, I and your mother and your brothers, to bow down to you to the earth?
And his brothers envied him, and his father kept the matter.
And his brothers went to herd their father's flock in Shechem.
And Yisroel said to Yosef: Are not your brothers herding in Shechem? Go, and I will send you to them. And he said to him: Here I am.
And he said to him: Go now, see the peace of your brothers and the peace of the flock, and bring me back word. And he sent him from the valley of Chevron, and he came to Shechem.
And a man found him, and behold, he was wandering in the field, and the man asked him, saying: What do you seek?
And he said: My brothers I seek; please tell me where they are herding.
And the man said: They have traveled from here, for I heard them saying: Let us go to Dotan. And Yosef went after his brothers, and found them in Dotan.
And they saw him from afar, and before he drew near to them, they conspired against him to kill him.
And they said, each man to his brother: Behold, this master of dreams comes.
And now, come, let us kill him, and cast him into one of the pits, and we will say: An evil beast devoured him, and we shall see what will become of his dreams.
And Reuven heard, and delivered him from their hand, and said: Let us not smite him mortally.
And Reuven said to them: Do not shed blood; cast him into this pit that is in the wilderness, and do not lay a hand on him, in order to deliver him from their hand, to bring him back to his father.
And it was, when Yosef came to his brothers, that they stripped Yosef of his tunic, the fine tunic that was upon him.
And they took him, and cast him into the pit, and the pit was empty, there was no water in it.

And they sat to eat bread, and they lifted their eyes, and saw, and behold, a caravan of Yishmaelim was coming from Gilad, and their camels were bearing spices and balm and labdanum, going to bring them down to Mitzrayim.
And Yehudah said to his brothers: What profit is it if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?
Come, let us sell him to the Yishmaelim, and let our hand not be upon him, for he is our brother, our flesh. And his brothers listened.
And Midyani men, merchants, passed by, and they pulled and lifted Yosef from the pit, and sold Yosef to the Yishmaelim for twenty silver pieces, and they brought Yosef to Mitzrayim.
And Reuven returned to the pit, and behold, Yosef was not in the pit, and he tore his garments.
And he returned to his brothers, and said: The boy is not there, and I, where shall I go?
And they took Yosef's tunic, and slaughtered a he-goat, and dipped the tunic in the blood.
And they sent the fine tunic, and brought it to their father, and said: This we have found; please identify whether it is your son's tunic or not.
And he identified it, and said: My son's tunic; an evil beast devoured him; Yosef was surely torn to pieces.
And Yackov tore his garments, and put sackcloth on his loins, and mourned his son many days.
And all his sons and all his daughters arose to console him, but he refused to be consoled, and said: For I will go down to my son, mourning, to the grave. And his father wept for him.
And the Midyanim sold him into Mitzrayim, to Potifar, an officer of Paroh, the chief of the executioners.
And it was at that time, that Yehudah went down from his brothers, and turned to a man, an Adulamite, and his name was Hira.
And Yehudah saw there the daughter of a Kena'ani man, and his name was Shua, and he took her, and came to her.
And she conceived, and bore a son, and he called his name Er.
And she conceived again, and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.
And she continued again, and bore a son, and she called his name Shelah, and he was in Keziv when she bore him.
And Yehudah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
And Er, Yehudah's firstborn, was wicked in the eyes of Havayah, and Havayah put him to death.
And Yehudah said to Onan: Come to your brother's wife, and perform levirate marriage with her, and raise up seed for your brother.
And Onan knew that the seed would not be his, and it was, when he came to his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, so as not to give seed to his brother.
And what he did was evil in the eyes of Havayah, and He put him to death also.

And Yehudah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law: Dwell as a widow in your father's house, until Shelah my son grows up, for he said: Lest he too die like his brothers. And Tamar went and dwelt in her father's house.
And the days increased, and the daughter of Shua, Yehudah's wife, died, and Yehudah was comforted, and went up to his sheepshearers, to Timna, he and Hira his friend the Adulamite.
And it was told to Tamar, saying: Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timna to shear his sheep.

And she removed the garments of her widowhood from upon her, and covered herself with a veil, and wrapped herself, and sat at the entrance of Einayim, which is on the way to Timna, for she saw that Shelah had grown, and she had not been given to him as a wife.
And Yehudah saw her, and thought her to be a harlot, for she had covered her face.
And he turned to her by the way, and said: Please, let me come to you, for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said: What will you give me, that you come to me?
And he said: I will send a kid from the flock. And she said: If you give a pledge until you send it.

And he said: What is the pledge that I should give you? And she said: Your signet, and your belt, and your staff that is in your hand. And he gave them to her, and came to her, and she conceived by him.
And she arose, and went, and removed her veil from upon her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.
And Yehudah sent the kid by the hand of his friend the Adulamite, to take the pledge from the hand of the woman, and he did not find her.
And he asked the men of her place, saying: Where is the harlot, who was at Einayim on the way? And they said: There was no harlot here.
And he returned to Yehudah, and said: I did not find her, and also the men of the place said: There was no harlot here.
And Yehudah said: Let her take it for herself, lest we become a laughingstock; behold, I sent this kid, and you did not find her.

And it was, after about three months, that it was told to Yehudah, saying: Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the harlot, and behold, she is also with child by harlotry. And Yehudah said: Bring her out, and let her be burned.
She was being brought out, and she sent to her father-in-law, saying: By the man whose these are, I am with child. And she said: Please identify whose are this signet, and belt, and staff.
And Yehudah identified them, and said: She is more righteous than I, because I did not give her to Shelah my son. And he did not know her again.
And it was at the time of her giving birth, and behold, twins were in her womb.
And it was, as she was giving birth, that one put out a hand, and the midwife took, and bound upon his hand a crimson thread, saying: This one came out first.
And it was, as he drew back his hand, that behold, his brother came out, and she said: What a breach you have breached for yourself! And he called his name Peretz.
And afterward his brother came out, on whose hand was the crimson thread, and he called his name Zerach.
And Yosef was brought down to Mitzrayim, and Potifar, an officer of Paroh, the chief of the executioners, a Mitzri man, bought him from the hand of the Yishmaelim, who had brought him down there.
And Havayah was with Yosef, and he was a successful man, and he was in the house of his master, the Mitzri.
And his master saw that Havayah was with him, and all that he did, Havayah made successful in his hand.
And Yosef found favor in his eyes, and he served him, and he appointed him over his house, and all that he had he placed in his hand.

And it was, from the time he appointed him over his house and over all that he had, that Havayah blessed the house of the Mitzri because of Yosef, and the blessing of Havayah was upon all that he had, in the house and in the field.
And he left all that he had in the hand of Yosef, and he did not know anything with him, except the bread that he ate. And Yosef was of fine form, and handsome.
And it was after these things, that his master's wife lifted her eyes to Yosef, and said: Lie with me.
And he refused, and said to his master's wife: Behold, my master does not know what is with me in the house, and all that he has he has placed in my hand.
There is no one greater in this house than I, and he has not withheld anything from me except you, because you are his wife, and how can I do this great evil, and sin against Elokim?
And it was, as she spoke to Yosef day after day, that he did not listen to her, to lie with her, to be with her.
And it was on a certain day, that he came into the house to do his work, and none of the men of the house were there in the house.
And she seized him by his garment, saying: Lie with me. And he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and went outside.
And it was, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and had fled outside,
that she summoned the men of her house, and spoke to them, saying: See, he brought us a Hebrew man to mock us; he came to me to lie with me, and I cried out with a loud voice.
And it was, when he heard that I lifted my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled, and went outside.
And she placed his garment beside her, until his master came to his house.
And she spoke to him according to these words, saying: The Hebrew servant, whom you brought to us, came to me to mock me.
And it was, as I lifted my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled outside.
And it was, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying: According to these words your servant did to me, that his anger burned.
And Yosef's master took him, and placed him in the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were imprisoned, and he was there in the prison.
And Havayah was with Yosef, and extended kindness to him, and gave him favor in the eyes of the chief of the prison.
And the chief of the prison placed in the hand of Yosef all the prisoners who were in the prison, and all that they did there, he did it.
The chief of the prison did not see anything that was in his hand, because Havayah was with him, and what he did, Havayah made successful.
And it was after these things, that the cupbearer of the king of Mitzrayim and the baker sinned against their master, against the king of Mitzrayim.
And Paroh was angry with his two officers, with the chief cupbearer and with the chief baker.
And he placed them in custody in the house of the chief of the executioners, in the prison, the place where Yosef was imprisoned.
And the chief of the executioners charged Yosef with them, and he served them, and they were in custody for days.

And they dreamed a dream, both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Mitzrayim, who were imprisoned in the prison.
And Yosef came to them in the morning, and saw them, and behold, they were distressed.
And he asked Paroh's officers who were with him in the custody of his master's house, saying: Why are your faces sad today?
And they said to him: We dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter for it. And Yosef said to them: Are not interpretations for Elokim? Please tell it to me.
And the chief cupbearer told his dream to Yosef, and said to him: In my dream, behold, a vine was before me.
And on the vine were three tendrils, and it was as though it budded, its blossom came up, and its clusters ripened into grapes.
And Paroh's cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Paroh's cup, and I gave the cup into Paroh's hand.
And Yosef said to him: This is its interpretation: The three tendrils are three days.
In another three days Paroh will lift up your head, and restore you to your post, and you will give Paroh's cup into his hand, as was the former manner when you were his cupbearer.
But remember me with you, when it is well with you, and please do kindness with me, and mention me to Paroh, and bring me out of this house.
For I was stolen, stolen from the land of the Hebrews, and here too I have done nothing, that they placed me in the pit.
And the chief baker saw that he had interpreted well, and he said to Yosef: I too, in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.
And in the uppermost basket was all kinds of food for Paroh, the work of a baker, and the birds were eating them from the basket, from upon my head.
And Yosef answered and said: This is its interpretation: The three baskets are three days.
In another three days Paroh will lift your head from upon you, and hang you on a tree, and the birds will eat your flesh from upon you.
And it was on the third day, Paroh's birthday, that he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.
And he restored the chief cupbearer to his cupbearing, and he gave the cup into Paroh's hand.
And the chief baker he hanged, as Yosef had interpreted for them.
And the chief cupbearer did not remember Yosef, and forgot him.
And it was at the end of two years, that Paroh dreamed, and behold, he was standing by the river.
And behold, from the river came up seven cows, fair of appearance and fat of flesh, and they grazed in the marsh.
And behold, seven other cows came up after them from the river, ill of appearance and lean of flesh, and stood beside the cows on the bank of the river.
And the cows, ill of appearance and lean of flesh, ate the seven cows, fair of appearance and fat, and Paroh awoke.
And he slept, and dreamed a second time, and behold, seven ears of grain came up on one stalk, full and good.
And behold, seven ears, thin and blasted by the east wind, sprouted after them.
And the thin ears swallowed the seven ears, full and good, and Paroh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.

And it was in the morning, that his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called all the magicians of Mitzrayim, and all its wise men, and Paroh told them his dream, and there was none who could interpret them for Paroh.
And the chief cupbearer spoke to Paroh, saying: My sins I mention today.
Paroh was angry with his servants, and placed me in custody in the house of the chief of the executioners, me and the chief baker.
And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he, each man according to the interpretation of his dream we dreamed.
And there with us was a Hebrew lad, a servant of the chief of the executioners, and we told him, and he interpreted our dreams for us, each man according to his dream he interpreted.
And it was, as he interpreted for us, so it was: me he restored to my post, and him he hanged.
And Paroh sent and called Yosef, and they rushed him from the pit, and he shaved, and changed his garments, and came to Paroh.
And Paroh said to Yosef: I dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it, and I heard of you, saying: You hear a dream to interpret it.
And Yosef answered Paroh, saying: Not by me; Elokim will answer the peace of Paroh.
And Paroh spoke to Yosef: In my dream, behold, I was standing on the bank of the river.
And behold, seven cows, fat of flesh and fair of appearance, came up from the river, and they grazed in the marsh.
And behold, seven other cows came up after them, poor, and very ill of appearance, and lean of flesh; I have not seen like them in all the land of Mitzrayim for ill appearance.
And the lean and ill cows ate the first seven fat cows.
And they came into their innards, and it was not known that they had come into their innards, and their appearance was ill as at first, and I awoke.
And I saw in my dream, and behold, seven ears came up on one stalk, full and good.
And behold, seven ears, withered, thin, blasted by the east wind, sprouted after them.
And the thin ears swallowed the seven good ears, and I told it to the magicians, and there was none who could tell me.
And Yosef said to Paroh: The dream of Paroh is one; what Elokim is about to do, He has told Paroh.
The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years; the dream is one.
And the seven lean and ill cows that came up after them are seven years, and the seven empty ears blasted by the east wind shall be seven years of famine.
That is the word that I spoke to Paroh: What Elokim is about to do, He has shown Paroh.
Behold, seven years of great plenty are coming in all the land of Mitzrayim.
And seven years of famine shall arise after them, and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Mitzrayim, and the famine shall consume the land.
And the plenty shall not be known in the land because of that famine afterward, for it shall be very severe.
And for the dream being repeated to Paroh twice, it is because the matter is determined by Elokim, and Elokim hastens to do it.
And now, let Paroh look for a man, discerning and wise, and set him over the land of Mitzrayim.
Let Paroh act, and appoint overseers over the land, and take a fifth of the land of Mitzrayim in the seven years of plenty.
And let them gather all the food of these good years that are coming, and heap up grain under the hand of Paroh, food in the cities, and guard it.
And the food shall be for a store for the land, for the seven years of famine that shall be in the land of Mitzrayim, and the land shall not be cut off by the famine.
And the thing was good in the eyes of Paroh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
And Paroh said to his servants: Can we find a man like this, in whom is the spirit of Elokim?
And Paroh said to Yosef: Since Elokim has made known to you all this, there is none discerning and wise like you.
You shall be over my house, and by your mouth shall all my people be sustained, only the throne I will be greater than you.
And Paroh said to Yosef: See, I have set you over all the land of Mitzrayim.
And Paroh removed his ring from his hand, and placed it on the hand of Yosef, and dressed him in garments of fine linen, and placed a gold chain on his neck.
And he had him ride in the second chariot that he had, and they cried before him: Kneel! And he set him over all the land of Mitzrayim.
And Paroh said to Yosef: I am Paroh, and without you no man shall lift his hand or his foot in all the land of Mitzrayim.
And Paroh called Yosef's name Tzafnas Paneach, and gave him Asnas, the daughter of Poti Fera, priest of On, for a wife, and Yosef went out over the land of Mitzrayim.
And Yosef was thirty years old when he stood before Paroh, king of Mitzrayim, and Yosef went out from before Paroh, and passed through all the land of Mitzrayim.
And the land produced in the seven years of plenty by handfuls.
And he gathered all the food of the seven years that were in the land of Mitzrayim, and placed food in the cities; the food of the field of the city that was around it he placed in it.
And Yosef heaped up grain like the sand of the sea, very much, until he ceased to count, for it was without number.
And to Yosef were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Asnas, the daughter of Poti Fera, priest of On, bore to him.
And Yosef called the name of the firstborn Menasheh, for Elokim has made me forget all my toil, and all my father's house.
And the name of the second he called Efrayim, for Elokim has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.
And the seven years of plenty that were in the land of Mitzrayim ended.
And the seven years of famine began to come, as Yosef had said, and there was famine in all the lands, but in all the land of Mitzrayim there was bread.
And all the land of Mitzrayim was hungry, and the people cried to Paroh for bread, and Paroh said to all the Mitzrim: Go to Yosef; what he says to you, do.
And the famine was on all the face of the earth, and Yosef opened all that was in them, and sold to the Mitzrim, and the famine was severe in the land of Mitzrayim.
And all the earth came to Mitzrayim to buy grain from Yosef, for the famine was severe in all the earth.
And Yackov saw that there was grain in Mitzrayim, and Yackov said to his sons: Why do you look at one another?
And he said: Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Mitzrayim; go down there, and buy for us from there, and we shall live, and not die.
And the ten brothers of Yosef went down to buy grain from Mitzrayim.
And Binyamin, Yosef's brother, Yackov did not send with his brothers, for he said: Lest disaster befall him.
And the sons of Yisroel came to buy among those who came, for the famine was in the land of Kena'an.
And Yosef was the ruler over the land, he was the one who sold to all the people of the land, and the brothers of Yosef came, and bowed down to him, faces to the earth.

And Yosef saw his brothers, and recognized them, and acted as a stranger to them, and spoke harshly with them, and said to them: From where have you come? And they said: From the land of Kena'an to buy food.
And Yosef recognized his brothers, and they did not recognize him.
And Yosef remembered the dreams that he dreamed about them, and said to them: You are spies; to see the nakedness of the land you have come.
And they said to him: No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.
We are all the sons of one man; we are honest men; your servants have not been spies.
And he said to them: No, but the nakedness of the land you have come to see.
And they said: Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Kena'an, and behold, the youngest is with our father today, and one is not.
And Yosef said to them: That is what I spoke to you, saying: You are spies.
By this you shall be tested: By the life of Paroh, you shall not go out from here, unless your youngest brother comes here.
Send one of you, and let him take your brother, and you shall be imprisoned, and your words shall be tested, whether truth is with you, and if not, by the life of Paroh, you are spies.
And he gathered them into custody for three days.
And Yosef said to them on the third day: Do this, and live; I fear Elokim.
If you are honest men, one of your brothers shall be imprisoned in your house of custody, and you, go, bring grain for the hunger of your houses.
And bring your youngest brother to me, and your words shall be verified, and you shall not die. And they did so.

And they said, each man to his brother: Truly we are guilty concerning our brother, that we saw the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen; therefore this distress has come upon us.
And Reuven answered them, saying: Did I not say to you, saying: Do not sin against the lad, and you did not listen? And behold, his blood is also required.
And they did not know that Yosef understood, for the interpreter was between them.
And he turned away from them, and wept, and returned to them, and spoke to them, and took Shimon from them, and bound him before their eyes.
And Yosef commanded, and they filled their vessels with grain, and returned each man's silver to his sack, and gave them provisions for the way, and he did so for them.
And they loaded their grain upon their donkeys, and went from there.
And one opened his sack to give feed to his donkey at the lodging place, and saw his silver, and behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.

And he said to his brothers: My silver has been returned, and behold, it is in my sack. And their hearts sank, and they trembled, each man to his brother, saying: What is this that Elokim has done to us?
And they came to Yackov their father, to the land of Kena'an, and told him all that had befallen them, saying:
The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly with us, and made us out to be spies of the land.
And we said to him: We are honest men; we have not been spies.
We are twelve brothers, the sons of our father; one is not, and the youngest is today with our father in the land of Kena'an.
And the man, the lord of the land, said to us: By this I shall know that you are honest men: One of your brothers leave with me, and take grain for the hunger of your houses, and go.
And bring your youngest brother to me, and I shall know that you are not spies, that you are honest men; your brother I will give to you, and you shall trade in the land.
And it was, as they emptied their sacks, that behold, each man's bundle of silver was in his sack, and they saw their bundles of silver, they and their father, and they were afraid.
