And Yackov their father said to them: You have bereaved me; Yosef is not, and Shimon is not, and Binyamin you would take; all these are upon me.
And Reuven spoke to his father, saying: My two sons you shall kill, if I do not bring him to you; place him in my hand, and I will bring him back to you.

And he said: My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left, and if disaster befalls him on the way that you go, then you will bring down my gray hairs in sorrow to the grave.
And the famine was severe in the land.
And it was, when they finished eating the grain that they had brought from Mitzrayim, that their father said to them: Return, buy us a little food.
And Yehudah spoke to him, saying: The man warned us, warning, saying: You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.
If you send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
And if you do not send him, we will not go down, for the man said to us: You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.
And Yisroel said: Why did you harm me, to tell the man that you have another brother?

And they said: The man asked, asking about us and about our kindred, saying: Is your father still alive? Do you have a brother? And we told him according to these words; could we know that he would say: Bring your brother down?
And Yehudah said to Yisroel his father: Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go, and live, and not die, both we, and you, and our children.
I will guarantee him; from my hand you shall seek him; if I do not bring him to you, and set him before you, then I shall have sinned to you all the days.
For had we not tarried, by now we would have returned twice.

And Yisroel their father said to them: If so, do this: Take of the choice fruits of the land in your vessels, and bring down a gift to the man, a little balm, and a little honey, spices, and labdanum, pistachios, and almonds.
And take double silver in your hand, and the silver that was returned in the mouth of your sacks, return in your hand; perhaps it was an oversight.
And take your brother, and arise, return to the man.
And El Shaddai will give you mercy before the man, and he will send with you your other brother, and Binyamin; and I, as I am bereaved, I am bereaved.
And the men took this gift, and double silver they took in their hand, and Binyamin, and arose, and went down to Mitzrayim, and stood before Yosef.
And Yosef saw Binyamin with them, and said to the one who was over his house: Bring the men into the house, and slaughter an animal, and prepare, for the men shall eat with me at noon.
And the man did as Yosef said, and the man brought the men into Yosef's house.

And the men were afraid, because they were brought into Yosef's house, and they said: Because of the silver that was returned in our sacks at first we are brought in, to roll himself upon us, and to fall upon us, and to take us as slaves, and our donkeys.
And they approached the man who was over Yosef's house, and spoke to him at the entrance of the house.
And they said: Please, my lord, we came down, came down at first to buy food.
And it was, when we came to the lodging place, and opened our sacks, that behold, each man's silver was in the mouth of his sack, our silver in its full weight, and we returned it in our hand.
And other silver we brought down in our hand to buy food; we do not know who placed our silver in our sacks.
And he said: Peace be to you, fear not; your Elokim, and the Elokim of your father, gave you treasure in your sacks; your silver came to me. And he brought Shimon out to them.
And the man brought the men into Yosef's house, and gave water, and they washed their feet, and he gave feed to their donkeys.
And they prepared the gift until Yosef came at noon, for they heard that they would eat bread there.
And Yosef came home, and they brought him the gift that was in their hand into the house, and bowed down to him to the earth.
And he asked them about their peace, and said: Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?
And they said: Your servant, our father, is well; he is still alive. And they bowed, and prostrated themselves.
And he lifted his eyes, and saw Binyamin his brother, the son of his mother, and said: Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me? And he said: Elokim be gracious to you, my son.
And Yosef hurried, for his mercy was aroused toward his brother, and he sought to weep, and entered the chamber, and wept there.
And he washed his face, and went out, and restrained himself, and said: Serve bread.
And they served for him alone, and for them alone, and for the Mitzrim who ate with him alone, for the Mitzrim cannot eat bread with the Hebrews, for it is an abomination to the Mitzrim.
And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his seniority, and the youngest according to his youth, and the men wondered, each man to his fellow.
And he sent portions from before him to them, and Binyamin's portion was five times the portions of all of them, and they drank, and were merry with him.
And he commanded the one who was over his house, saying: Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and place each man's silver in the mouth of his sack.
And my goblet, the silver goblet, place in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, and the silver of his grain. And he did according to the word of Yosef that he had spoken.
The morning shone, and the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
They had gone out of the city, they had not gone far, and Yosef said to the one who was over his house: Arise, pursue the men, and overtake them, and say to them: Why have you repaid evil for good?
Is this not the one in which my lord drinks, and with which he indeed divines? You have done evil in what you did.
And he overtook them, and spoke to them these words.
And they said to him: Why does my lord speak such words? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing.
Behold, the silver that we found in the mouth of our sacks we returned to you from the land of Kena'an, and how shall we steal from the house of your lord silver or gold?
With whomever of your servants it is found, he shall die, and we too shall be slaves to my lord.
And he said: Now also, according to your words, so shall it be: He with whom it is found shall be my slave, and you shall be innocent.
And each man hurried, and lowered his sack to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
And he searched, beginning with the eldest, and with the youngest he ended, and the goblet was found in Binyamin's sack.
And they tore their garments, and each man loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city.
And Yehudah and his brothers came to Yosef's house, and he was still there, and they fell before him to the ground.
And Yosef said to them: What is this deed that you have done? Did you not know that a man like me indeed divines?

And Yehudah said: What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak, and how shall we justify ourselves? Elokim has found the iniquity of your servants; behold, we are slaves to my lord, both we, and he in whose hand the goblet was found.
And he said: Far be it from me to do this; the man in whose hand the goblet was found, he shall be my slave, and you, go up in peace to your father.
And Yehudah approached him, and said: Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in the ears of my lord, and let your anger not burn against your servant, for you are like Paroh.
My lord asked his servants, saying: Do you have a father or a brother?
And we said to my lord: We have an old father, and a young son of his old age, and his brother is dead, and he alone remains of his mother, and his father loves him.
And you said to your servants: Bring him down to me, and I will set my eye upon him.
And we said to my lord: The lad cannot leave his father, for if he leaves his father, he will die.
And you said to your servants: If your youngest brother does not come down with you, you shall not see my face again.
And it was, when we went up to your servant, my father, that we told him the words of my lord.
And our father said: Return, buy us a little food.
And we said: We cannot go down; if our youngest brother is with us, we will go down, for we cannot see the man's face, unless our youngest brother is with us.
And your servant, my father, said to us: You know that my wife bore me two sons.
And the one went out from me, and I said: Surely he was torn to pieces, and I have not seen him since.
And if you take this one also from me, and disaster befalls him, then you will bring down my gray hairs in sorrow to the grave.
And now, when I come to your servant, my father, and the lad is not with us, and his soul is bound with his soul,
it shall be, when he sees that the lad is not, that he will die, and your servants will bring down the gray hairs of your servant, our father, in sorrow to the grave.
For your servant guaranteed the lad to my father, saying: If I do not bring him to you, then I shall have sinned to my father all the days.
And now, please, let your servant remain instead of the lad, a slave to my lord, and let the lad go up with his brothers.
For how shall I go up to my father, and the lad is not with me? Lest I see the evil that shall find my father.
And Yosef could not restrain himself before all who stood by him, and he cried: Remove every man from me. And no man stood with him when Yosef made himself known to his brothers.
And he gave his voice in weeping, and the Mitzrim heard, and the house of Paroh heard.
And Yosef said to his brothers: I am Yosef; is my father still alive? And his brothers could not answer him, for they were terrified before him.
And Yosef said to his brothers: Please come near to me. And they came near, and he said: I am Yosef your brother, whom you sold into Mitzrayim.
And now, do not be sad, and do not be angry with yourselves that you sold me here, for Elokim sent me before you for sustenance.
For these two years the famine has been in the midst of the land, and there are still five years in which there shall be neither plowing nor harvest.
And Elokim sent me before you to set for you a remnant in the land, and to keep you alive for a great deliverance.
And now, it was not you who sent me here, but Elokim, and He made me a father to Paroh, and a lord for all his house, and a ruler over all the land of Mitzrayim.
Hurry, and go up to my father, and say to him: Thus says your son Yosef: Elokim has made me lord over all Mitzrayim; come down to me, do not tarry.
And you shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near me, you, and your sons, and your sons' sons, and your flocks, and your cattle, and all that you have.
And I will sustain you there, for there are still five years of famine, lest you become poor, you, and your household, and all that you have.
And behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Binyamin, that my mouth is speaking to you.
And you shall tell my father all my glory in Mitzrayim, and all that you have seen, and hurry, and bring my father down here.
And he fell upon the neck of Binyamin his brother, and wept, and Binyamin wept upon his neck.
And he kissed all his brothers, and wept upon them, and afterward his brothers spoke with him.
And the report was heard in Paroh's house, saying: Yosef's brothers have come, and it was good in the eyes of Paroh, and in the eyes of his servants.
And Paroh said to Yosef: Say to your brothers: Do this: Load your beasts, and go, come to the land of Kena'an.
And take your father and your households, and come to me, and I will give you the best of the land of Mitzrayim, and you shall eat the fat of the land.
And you are commanded: Do this: Take wagons for yourselves from the land of Mitzrayim, for your little ones and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.
And your eye shall not spare your vessels, for the best of all the land of Mitzrayim is yours.
And the sons of Yisroel did so, and Yosef gave them wagons by the command of Paroh, and gave them provisions for the way.
To all of them he gave, to each man, changes of garments, and to Binyamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver, and five changes of garments.
And to his father he sent as follows: Ten donkeys laden with the best of Mitzrayim, and ten she-donkeys laden with grain, and bread, and food for his father for the way.
And he sent his brothers away, and they went, and he said to them: Do not quarrel on the way.
And they went up from Mitzrayim, and came to the land of Kena'an, to Yackov their father.
And they told him, saying: Yosef is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Mitzrayim. And his heart fainted, for he did not believe them.
And they spoke to him all the words of Yosef that he had spoken to them, and he saw the wagons that Yosef had sent to carry him, and the spirit of Yackov their father revived.
And Yisroel said: It is enough; Yosef my son is still alive; I will go and see him before I die.
And Yisroel journeyed, and all that he had, and came to Be'er Sheva, and slaughtered sacrifices to the Elokim of his father Yitzchak.
And Elokim spoke to Yisroel in the visions of the night, and said: Yackov, Yackov. And he said: Here I am.
And He said: I am El, the Elokim of your father; do not fear to go down to Mitzrayim, for I will make you a great nation there.
I will go down with you to Mitzrayim, and I will also bring you up, bring you up, and Yosef shall place his hand upon your eyes.
And Yackov arose from Be'er Sheva, and the sons of Yisroel carried Yackov their father, and their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons that Paroh had sent to carry him.
And they took their livestock, and their property that they had acquired in the land of Kena'an, and came to Mitzrayim, Yackov, and all his seed with him.
His sons, and his sons' sons with him, his daughters, and his sons' daughters, and all his seed he brought with him to Mitzrayim.
And these are the names of the sons of Yisroel who came to Mitzrayim, Yackov and his sons: The firstborn of Yackov, Reuven.
And the sons of Reuven: Chanoch, and Palu, and Chetzron, and Karmi.
And the sons of Shimon: Yemuel, and Yamin, and Ohad, and Yachin, and Tzochar, and Shaul, the son of the Kena'ani woman.
And the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kehas, and Merari.
And the sons of Yehudah: Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Peretz, and Zerach; and Er and Onan died in the land of Kena'an. And the sons of Peretz were Chetzron and Chamul.
And the sons of Yissachar: Tola, and Puvah, and Yov, and Shimron.
And the sons of Zevulun: Sered, and Elon, and Yachle'el.
These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Yackov in Padan Aram, and Dinah his daughter; all the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty-three.
And the sons of Gad: Tzifyon, and Chaggi, Shuni, and Etzbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
And the sons of Asher: Yimnah, and Yishvah, and Yishvi, and Beriah, and Serach their sister. And the sons of Beriah: Chever and Malkiel.
These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Lavan gave to Leah his daughter, and she bore these to Yackov, sixteen souls.
The sons of Rachel, Yackov's wife: Yosef and Binyamin.
And to Yosef were born in the land of Mitzrayim, whom Asnas, the daughter of Poti Fera, priest of On, bore to him, Menasheh and Efrayim.
And the sons of Binyamin: Bela, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, Echi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Chuppim, and Ard.
These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Yackov; all the souls were fourteen.
And the sons of Dan: Chushim.
And the sons of Naftali: Yachtze'el, and Guni, and Yetzer, and Shillem.
These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Lavan gave to Rachel his daughter, and she bore these to Yackov; all the souls were seven.
All the souls who came with Yackov to Mitzrayim, who came out of his loins, besides the wives of Yackov's sons, all the souls were sixty-six.
And the sons of Yosef, who were born to him in Mitzrayim, were two souls; all the souls of the house of Yackov who came to Mitzrayim were seventy.
And Yehudah he sent before him to Yosef, to show the way before him to Goshen, and they came to the land of Goshen.
And Yosef harnessed his chariot, and went up to meet Yisroel his father, to Goshen, and appeared to him, and fell upon his neck, and wept upon his neck for a long time.
And Yisroel said to Yosef: Let me die now, after I have seen your face, for you are still alive.
And Yosef said to his brothers, and to his father's house: I will go up, and tell Paroh, and say to him: My brothers, and my father's house, who were in the land of Kena'an, have come to me.
And the men are shepherds, for they are men of livestock, and their flocks, and their cattle, and all that they have, they have brought.
And it shall be, when Paroh calls you, and says: What is your work?

And you shall say: Your servants have been men of livestock from our youth until now, both we and our fathers, in order that you may dwell in the land of Goshen, for every shepherd is an abomination to the Mitzrim.

And Yosef went and told Paroh, and said: My father and my brothers, and their flocks, and their cattle, and all that they have, have come from the land of Kena'an, and behold, they are in the land of Goshen.
And from among his brothers he took five men, and presented them before Paroh.
And Paroh said to his brothers: What is your work? And they said to Paroh: Your servants are shepherds, both we and our fathers.

And they said to Paroh: To sojourn in the land we have come, for there is no pasture for the flocks of your servants, for the famine is severe in the land of Kena'an, and now, please, let your servants dwell in the land of Goshen.
And Paroh spoke to Yosef, saying: Your father and your brothers have come to you.

The land of Mitzrayim is before you; in the best of the land settle your father and your brothers; they shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and if you know that there are capable men among them, then set them as chiefs of the livestock that are mine.
And Yosef brought Yackov his father, and stood him before Paroh, and Yackov blessed Paroh.
And Paroh said to Yackov: How many are the days of the years of your life?

And Yackov said to Paroh: The days of the years of my sojournings are one hundred and thirty years; few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their sojournings.
And Yackov blessed Paroh, and went out from before Paroh.
And Yosef settled his father and his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Mitzrayim, in the best of the land, in the land of Raamses, as Paroh had commanded.
And Yosef sustained his father, and his brothers, and all his father's house, with bread, according to the little ones.
And there was no bread in all the land, for the famine was very severe, and the land of Mitzrayim and the land of Kena'an languished because of the famine.
And Yosef gathered all the silver that was found in the land of Mitzrayim and in the land of Kena'an, for the grain that they were buying, and Yosef brought the silver to Paroh's house.
And the silver was spent in the land of Mitzrayim and in the land of Kena'an, and all the Mitzrim came to Yosef, saying: Give us bread, for why should we die before you, because the silver is spent?
And Yosef said: Give your livestock, and I will give to you for your livestock, if the silver is spent.

And they brought their livestock to Yosef, and Yosef gave them bread for the horses, and for the livestock of the flocks, and for the livestock of the cattle, and for the donkeys, and he sustained them with bread for all their livestock in that year.

And that year ended, and they came to him in the second year, and said to him: We will not hide from my lord that the silver is spent, and the livestock of the cattle are my lord's; nothing is left before my lord except our bodies and our land.

Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land shall be servants to Paroh, and give seed, and we shall live, and not die, and the land shall not be desolate.
And Yosef bought all the land of Mitzrayim for Paroh, for the Mitzrim sold each man his field, for the famine was severe upon them, and the land became Paroh's.
And the people he moved to the cities, from one end of the border of Mitzrayim to its other end.
Only the land of the priests he did not buy, for the priests had a portion from Paroh, and they ate their portion that Paroh gave them; therefore they did not sell their land.
And Yosef said to the people: Behold, I have bought you today, and your land, for Paroh; here is seed for you, and sow the land.

And it shall be, at the harvests, that you shall give a fifth to Paroh, and four parts shall be yours, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for those in your houses, and for food for your little ones.
And they said: You have kept us alive; let us find favor in the eyes of my lord, and we will be servants to Paroh.
And Yosef made it a statute to this day concerning the land of Mitzrayim, that Paroh shall have the fifth; only the land of the priests alone did not become Paroh's.
And Yisroel dwelt in the land of Mitzrayim, in the land of Goshen, and they took possession of it, and were fruitful, and multiplied exceedingly.
And Yackov lived in the land of Mitzrayim seventeen years, and the days of Yackov, the years of his life, were one hundred years and forty years and seven years.

And the days of Yisroel drew near to die, and he called his son Yosef, and said to him: If now I have found favor in your eyes, please place your hand under my thigh, and do kindness and truth with me; please do not bury me in Mitzrayim.
And I shall lie with my fathers, and you shall carry me from Mitzrayim, and bury me in their burial place. And he said: I will do according to your word.
And he said: Swear to me. And he swore to him, and Yisroel bowed himself upon the head of the bed.
And it was after these things, that it was said to Yosef: Behold, your father is ill. And he took his two sons with him, Menasheh and Efrayim.
And it was told to Yackov, and said: Behold, your son Yosef is coming to you. And Yisroel strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.
And Yackov said to Yosef: El Shaddai appeared to me in Luz, in the land of Kena'an, and blessed me.
And He said to me: Behold, I will make you fruitful, and multiply you, and make you an assembly of peoples, and give this land to your seed after you as an everlasting possession.
And now, your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Mitzrayim before I came to you to Mitzrayim, are mine; Efrayim and Menasheh, like Reuven and Shimon, shall be mine.
And your offspring that you beget after them shall be yours; by the name of their brothers they shall be called in their inheritance.

And as for me, when I came from Padan, Rachel died upon me in the land of Kena'an on the way, when there was still a distance of land to come to Efras, and I buried her there on the way to Efras, which is Beit Lechem.
And Yisroel saw Yosef's sons, and said: Who are these?
And Yosef said to his father: They are my sons, whom Elokim has given me here. And he said: Please bring them to me, and I will bless them.
And the eyes of Yisroel were heavy from age, he could not see, and he brought them near to him, and he kissed them, and embraced them.
And Yisroel said to Yosef: I did not think to see your face, and behold, Elokim has shown me your seed also.
And Yosef took them from his knees, and bowed down, his face to the earth.
And Yosef took the two of them, Efrayim in his right hand, to the left of Yisroel, and Menasheh in his left hand, to the right of Yisroel, and brought them near to him.

And Yisroel stretched out his right hand, and placed it upon the head of Efrayim, and he was the younger, and his left hand upon the head of Menasheh, crossing his hands, for Menasheh was the firstborn.
And he blessed Yosef, and said: The Elokim before whom my fathers Avraham and Yitzchak walked, the Elokim who shepherds me from my beginning until this day,

the angel who redeems me from all evil, may he bless the lads, and let my name be called upon them, and the name of my fathers Avraham and Yitzchak, and let them multiply abundantly in the midst of the earth.

And Yosef saw that his father placed his right hand upon the head of Efrayim, and it was evil in his eyes, and he took hold of his father's hand, to remove it from the head of Efrayim to the head of Menasheh.
And Yosef said to his father: Not so, my father, for this is the firstborn; place your right hand upon his head.

And his father refused, and said: I know, my son, I know; he too shall become a people, and he too shall be great, but his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become the fullness of nations.
And he blessed them on that day, saying: By you shall Yisroel bless, saying: Elokim make you like Efrayim and like Menasheh. And he placed Efrayim before Menasheh.
And Yisroel said to Yosef: Behold, I am dying, and Elokim shall be with you, and bring you back to the land of your fathers.
And I have given you one portion above your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Emori with my sword and with my bow.
And Yackov called his sons, and said: Gather yourselves, and I will tell you what shall befall you at the end of days.
Assemble, and hear, sons of Yackov, and listen to Yisroel your father.
Reuven, you are my firstborn, my strength, and the first of my power, excelling in dignity, and excelling in might.
Unstable as water, you shall not excel, for you went up to your father's bed; then you defiled it, he who went up to my couch.
Shimon and Levi are brothers; weapons of violence are their swords.
Into their council my soul shall not come; with their assembly my honor shall not be joined, for in their anger they slew a man, and in their will they hamstrung an ox.
Cursed be their anger, for it is fierce, and their wrath, for it is cruel; I will divide them in Yackov, and scatter them in Yisroel.
Yehudah, you your brothers shall praise; your hand shall be on the neck of your enemies; the sons of your father shall bow down to you.
A lion's whelp is Yehudah; from the prey, my son, you have gone up; he crouched, he lay down like a lion, and like a lioness, who shall rouse him?
The scepter shall not depart from Yehudah, nor the lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh comes, and to him shall be the obedience of the peoples.
He binds his foal to the vine, and his donkey's colt to the choice vine; he washes his garments in wine, and his clothing in the blood of grapes.
His eyes are redder than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.
Zevulun shall dwell at the shore of the seas, and he shall be a shore for ships, and his border shall be to Tzidon.
Yissachar is a strong-boned donkey, lying between the sheepfolds.
And he saw rest, that it was good, and the land, that it was pleasant, and bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a servant under tribute.
Dan shall judge his people, as one of the tribes of Yisroel.
Dan shall be a serpent on the way, a viper on the path, that bites the horse's heels, and its rider falls backward.
For Your salvation I wait, Havayah.
Gad, a troop shall troop upon him, and he shall troop upon their heel.
From Asher, his bread shall be fat, and he shall give royal dainties.
Naftali is a doe let loose, who gives goodly words.
Yosef is a fruitful son, a fruitful son by a spring, daughters stride over the wall.
They embittered him, and shot at him, and hated him, the archers.
And his bow remained firm, and the arms of his hands were made strong, by the hands of the Mighty One of Yackov, from there is the Shepherd, the Stone of Yisroel.
From the El of your father, and He shall help you, and El Shaddai, and He shall bless you, with blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lies below, blessings of breasts and of womb.

The blessings of your father have prevailed over the blessings of my parents, to the utmost bound of the everlasting hills; they shall be on the head of Yosef, and on the crown of the head of the one set apart from his brothers.
Binyamin is a wolf that tears; in the morning he devours the prey, and in the evening he divides the spoil.
All these are the tribes of Yisroel, twelve, and this is what their father spoke to them, and he blessed them, each man according to his blessing he blessed them.
And he commanded them, and said to them: I am to be gathered to my people; bury me with my fathers, in the cave that is in the field of Efron the Chiti.
In the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, in the land of Kena'an, which Avraham bought with the field from Efron the Chiti, for a possession of a burial place.
There they buried Avraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Yitzchak and Rivkah his wife; and there I buried Leah.
The field and the cave that is in it were bought from the children of Ches.
And Yackov finished commanding his sons, and gathered his feet into the bed, and expired, and was gathered to his people.
And Yosef fell upon the face of his father, and wept upon him, and kissed him.
And Yosef commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father, and the physicians embalmed Yisroel.
And forty days were fulfilled for him, for so are fulfilled the days of those who are embalmed, and the Mitzrim wept for him seventy days.
And the days of his weeping passed, and Yosef spoke to the house of Paroh, saying: If now I have found favor in your eyes, please speak in the ears of Paroh, saying:

My father made me swear, saying: Behold, I am dying; in my grave that I dug for myself in the land of Kena'an, there shall you bury me. Now, let me go up, please, and bury my father, and I will return.
And Paroh said: Go up, and bury your father, as he made you swear.
And Yosef went up to bury his father, and all the servants of Paroh went up with him, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Mitzrayim.
And all the house of Yosef, and his brothers, and his father's house; only their little ones, and their flocks, and their cattle, they left in the land of Goshen.
And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen, and the camp was very great.
And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Yarden, and mourned there with a great and very sore mourning, and he observed mourning for his father seven days.

And the inhabitants of the land, the Kena'ani, saw the mourning in the threshing floor of Atad, and said: This is a grievous mourning for the Mitzrim; therefore its name was called Avel Mitzrayim, which is beyond the Yarden.
And his sons did to him as he had commanded them.

And his sons carried him to the land of Kena'an, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Avraham bought with the field for a possession of a burial place, from Efron the Chiti, before Mamre.
And Yosef returned to Mitzrayim, he, and his brothers, and all who went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.
And the brothers of Yosef saw that their father was dead, and said: Perhaps Yosef will hate us, and will surely repay us all the evil that we did to him.
And they sent to Yosef, saying: Your father commanded before his death, saying:

Thus shall you say to Yosef: Please forgive, please, the transgression of your brothers, and their sin, for they did evil to you. And now, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the Elokim of your father. And Yosef wept when they spoke to him.
And his brothers also went, and fell before him, and said: Behold, we are your slaves.
And Yosef said to them: Fear not, for am I in the place of Elokim?
And you, you thought evil against me; Elokim thought it for good, in order to do as it is this day, to keep many people alive.
And now, fear not; I will sustain you and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spoke to their hearts.
And Yosef dwelt in Mitzrayim, he, and his father's house, and Yosef lived one hundred and ten years.
And Yosef saw Efrayim's children of the third generation; the children of Machir, the son of Menasheh, were also born upon Yosef's knees.
And Yosef said to his brothers: I am dying, and Elokim will surely remember you, and bring you up from this land to the land that He swore to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yackov.
And Yosef made the children of Yisroel swear, saying: Elokim will surely remember you, and you shall carry up my bones from here.
And Yosef died, a hundred and ten years old, and they embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Mitzrayim.
